Field Type Description direct string The peer's current endpoint as the hub's kernel sees it, in canonical [v6]:port form. handshake_age integer Seconds between the hub's clock at snapshot time and the peer's last handshake, never negative. Omitted if the peer has never completed a handshake.

The body reflects the snapshot taken on the hub's last cycle, not a live read.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
The server checks the request line in this order.

Status Condition Body 400 Bad Request The first line is not <METHOD> <path> HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1, with an uppercase method { "error": "bad request" } 405 Method Not Allowed Method is not GET (including HEAD) { "error": "method not allowed" } 404 Not Found Path is not exactly /peers (a query string also gives 404) { "error": "not found" } 200 OK GET /peers The snapshot

Every reply is HTTP/1.0 with these headers, after which the server closes the connection:

Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: <bytes>
Connection: close

docs.title: Connection handling
docs.text:
• One request per connection. The request is complete at the first blank line ( or ); anything after it is ignored.
  • A request larger than 4096 bytes without a blank line is closed without a reply.
  • A connection that has not completed its request within 2 seconds is closed without a reply.
  • At most 2 connections from one source address are open at once, the address compared in its canonical form. A third from the same address is served, and that address's oldest connection is closed without a reply.
  • At most 16 connections are open at once. When all 16 are open, a new connection from another address is served, and the oldest open connection is closed without a reply.
  • Every open connection is one still waiting for its request: an answered one is closed at once. So a client that opens connections and sends nothing cannot keep a client from another address out; at worst it takes a slow client's place, and that client's request fails like a timeout. A spoke sends its request as soon as it connects.
  • Requests never run a command on the hub; they are answered from memory.

docs.title: Spoke-side validation
docs.text:
A spoke fetches the URL with an HTTP GET. The fetch counts as failed, with the listed error code, in these cases:

Condition Code Detail The URL cannot be parsed DISCOVERY_FETCH_FAILED invalid url <url> The connection or request cannot start DISCOVERY_FETCH_FAILED cannot connect A transport error occurs DISCOVERY_FETCH_FAILED uclient error <code> No complete response within 5 seconds DISCOVERY_FETCH_FAILED timeout The body exceeds 65536 bytes DISCOVERY_FETCH_FAILED response too large The HTTP status is not 200 DISCOVERY_FETCH_FAILED HTTP <status> The body is not a JSON object DISCOVERY_INVALID_JSON — The object has more than 64 entries DISCOVERY_INVALID_PEERS too many peers A key is not a WireGuard public key DISCOVERY_INVALID_PEERS invalid public key An entry is invalid (see below) DISCOVERY_INVALID_PEERS the entry's key

An entry is valid when it is an object whose direct is a valid [v6]:port endpoint with port 1–65535, and whose handshake_age, if present, is an integer of zero or more. Other fields are ignored.

One invalid entry rejects the whole payload. A valid entry whose address could not be a direct path, one that is unspecified (::), loopback (::1), multicast (ff00::/8), link-local (fe80::/10), IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), IPv4-compatible (::/96), NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48) or discard-only (100::/64), is left out alone, and the rest of the payload is taken: it is one peer's address, not a broken payload, and that peer simply has no candidate. The same rule applies to the cache when it is loaded. On any failure the spoke keeps its previous map, sets discovery.fresh to false in the status and logs discovery failed: <code> (<detail>).

A valid payload replaces the spoke's map and is written to /var/run/wgpathd/cache.json. Entries whose key is not one of the spoke's managed peers are ignored. The handshake_age field is accepted but not used in any decision.

Every cycle, before probing, the spoke also refuses a peer's candidate that this router must not take as that peer's direct endpoint, whose address is:

Reason The address is own address an address of this router relay address the host of the relay in the peer's peer section tunnel address the tunnel in the peer's peer section routes into <iface> routed out of mesh_iface or hub_iface, where a WireGuard endpoint would loop into a tunnel

A refused candidate is neither probed nor trialed: a peer in RELAY stays there, unless it roams to a direct address by itself. The refusal is logged when it starts or its reason changes, and when it ends, and the peer's status shows it in candidate_refused. A candidate whose route cannot be looked up is not refused: its probes fail on their own. The refusal applies to candidates only; an authenticated roam is taken as before.

docs.title: Documentation Publishing
docs.text: The documentation is published with mike to the gh-pages branch, one version per minor release, by the docs workflow in .github/workflows/docs.yml. The make targets that build and test it locally are in Make targets. For the reasons behind this design, see About versioned documentation.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
Event Ref Job Publishes Version title Push of a tag v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+, for example v0.2.1 publish version X.Y X.Y.Z, the tag without its v Push to a branch docs/[0-9]+.[0-9]+, for example docs/0.2 publish version X.Y, if the docs-only guard passes the newest vX.Y.* tag without its v Push to a branch main build nothing — Pull request into main build nothing — Manual run (workflow_dispatch) the input ref: a release tag vX.Y.Z or a branch docs/X.Y publish as for a push of that ref as for a push of that ref

Branch pushes and pull requests start the workflow only when they change at least one of these paths. Tag pushes and manual runs always start it.

  • docs/**
  • mkdocs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml
  • devenv/gh-pages/**
  • devenv/scripts/docs-*.sh
  • devenv/services/docs/**
  • test/docs/**
  • .github/workflows/docs.yml

Nothing else publishes: main, pull requests and pre-release tags such as v0.3.0-rc1 never reach gh-pages.

docs.title: build
docs.text:
Runs on pull requests and on pushes to main.

  1. make -C docs build: strict build with mkdocs.yml.
  2. make -C docs build-mike: strict build with mkdocs.mike.yml.
  3. make -C docs test: the tests in test/docs/.

docs.title: publish
docs.text:
Runs on release tags, docs/* branches and manual runs. REF is the manual run's ref input, or else the pushed ref.

  1. Checks out REF with its full history and tags.
  2. Installs Python 3.12 and devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt with pip.
  3. Sets the git committer to github-actions[bot].
  4. mkdocs build --strict --config-file mkdocs.mike.yml.
  5. devenv/scripts/docs-publish.sh "$REF".

docs.title: Permissions and concurrency
docs.text:
Setting Value Workflow permissions contents: read publish permissions contents: write publish concurrency group gh-pages, with cancel-in-progress: false

One publish job runs at a time; a later one waits. GitHub keeps at most one waiting job per concurrency group: a newer one cancels the one already waiting.

docs.title: The latest rule
docs.text:
A publish of version X.Y also points latest to X.Y, and makes latest the default version, only if X.Y is the newest of the version folders already on gh-pages together with X.Y itself, compared with sort -V: 0.10 is newer than 0.9. Otherwise latest stays where it is. The first publish always takes latest.

The script prints which case applied:

publishing 0.10 (0.10.0) as latest
publishing 0.9 (0.9.1); latest stays on 0.10

docs.title: Site layout
docs.text:
The published site on gh-pages:

Path Written by Content /X.Y/ mike One folder per minor, without a v: 0.9, 0.10. /latest/ mike A full copy of the newest minor's folder (alias_type: copy), not a symlink or a redirect. /versions.json mike The versions, their titles and aliases, for the version selector. /index.html mike Redirects to /latest/ (mike set-default latest). /404.html docs-publish.sh Copy of devenv/gh-pages/404.html. See below. /.nojekyll docs-publish.sh Empty. Tells GitHub Pages to serve the files as they are.

Every page carries a version selector. With site_url set, its canonical URL is the same page under /latest/ (canonical_version: latest). Pages of a version that is not latest show a banner, docs/overrides/main.html:

You are reading the documentation of an older release. Go to the latest.

The link goes to the site's root, which redirects to /latest/.

docs.title: 404 redirect
docs.text:
GitHub Pages serves /404.html for every missing path. Its script redirects /<site>/<path> to /<site>/latest/<path>, keeping the query string and the #anchor. /<site> and /<site>/ go to /<site>/latest/.

It does not redirect, and shows "Page not found", when the first segment after /<site>/ is latest, dev or a version X.Y, or when the path is /. The first path segment is always taken as the site, so the redirect works only on a project site, https://<user>.github.io/<site>/.

docs.title: Docs-only guard
docs.text:
devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh runs before every publish of a docs/X.Y branch, whether pushed or run manually. It does not run for release tags. It checks the checked-out commit, HEAD, against the release tag of its minor:

  1. The tag is the newest tag of the form vX.Y.Z with the branch's X.Y, by sort -V: v0.9.10 is newer than v0.9.9. Other tags, such as v0.9.11-rc1, are ignored.
  2. The tag must be an ancestor of HEAD.
  3. HEAD may differ from the tag only in these files: anything under the top-level docs/, mkdocs.yml, mkdocs.mike.yml. A docs/ folder anywhere else, such as src/docs/, does not count.

On success the guard prints the tag, which becomes the version's title. On failure it prints one of these messages on stderr, exits 1, and nothing is published:

Message Cause not a docs/X.Y branch: <ref> The first argument is not a docs/ branch. not a release tag vX.Y.Z or a docs/X.Y branch: <ref> The branch is docs/ but not docs/X.Y. docs/X.Y has no vX.Y.* release tag No release tag of that minor exists. <tag> is not a X.Y release The tag given as the second argument is of another minor. not a release tag: <tag> The second argument does not start with v. <tag> is not an ancestor of docs/X.Y The branch does not contain its newest release tag, for example after a patch release it has not moved to. docs/X.Y changes files outside docs/: <files>; code fixes need a release The branch changes other files than the docs. The files are listed, space-separated.

For example:

docs/0.2 changes files outside docs/: src/wgpathd/daemon.uc; code fixes need a release

To run it locally, check out the branch, make sure the release tags are fetched, and pass the branch name:

devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh docs/0.2

docs.title: Links to the documentation
docs.text:
Where the link is It points to Always-current places: the README, the repository's homepage, forum posts <site_url>latest/... CHANGELOG.md <site_url>X.Y/..., the minor of the section the link is in Release notes <site_url>X.Y/..., the minor of the release Shipped files: everything under files/ and src/, and openwrt/wgpathd/Makefile (including URL:=) <site_url>X.Y/..., the package's current minor Pages of the documentation Relative paths, never the site's URL

site_url is the site's base URL without a version, set in mkdocs.yml, for example https://<user>.github.io/wgpathd/.

docs.title: Link check
docs.text:
make lint runs devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh, which checks every pinned link, <site_url><X.Y>/, in the shipped files and in CHANGELOG.md:

  • site_url is read from mkdocs.yml, with or without quotes; a missing trailing / is added. While site_url is unset, nothing is checked and the check passes.
  • In shipped files the minor must be the one of PKG_VERSION in openwrt/wgpathd/Makefile: PKG_VERSION:=0.1.0 requires 0.1.
  • In CHANGELOG.md the minor must be the one of the enclosing ## [X.Y.Z] heading. Any other ## heading, such as ## [Unreleased], and the text before the first ## heading allow no pinned link at all. ### headings do not change the section.
  • Links to latest/ and links under other URLs are not checked.

CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog: ## [Unreleased] on top, then one ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section per release, newest first. Only the ## [X.Y.Z] part of the heading is read.

A failure prints every wrong link and exits 1:

pinned docs links to the wrong version:
files/etc/config/wgpathd:1: https://example.org/wgpathd/0.9/ (expected 0.10)
CHANGELOG.md:5: https://example.org/wgpathd/0.10/ (outside a release section)

docs.title: Files and scripts
docs.text: File Role .github/workflows/docs.yml The docs workflow: triggers, jobs. mkdocs.yml The site. Has no mike settings; make -C docs build and serve use it. mkdocs.mike.yml The versioned site: inherits mkdocs.yml and adds the search and mike plugins (canonical_version: latest, alias_type: copy), the version selector (extra.version.provider: mike) and the theme overrides in docs/overrides/. Used by build-mike and by the publish job. docs/overrides/main.html The outdated-version banner. devenv/gh-pages/404.html The 404 redirect, copied to the root of gh-pages on every publish. devenv/services/docs/Dockerfile The docs tools image, wgpathd-docs: the mkdocs-material image plus requirements.txt, git, coreutils and Node. devenv/services/docs/requirements.txt Pinned mkdocs-material and mike, for the tools image and the publish job. devenv/scripts/docs-version.sh Maps a ref to its docs version. devenv/scripts/docs-guard.sh The docs-only guard. devenv/scripts/docs-publish.sh Publishes one version. devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh The link check. test/docs/ Tests of the four scripts and of the 404 redirect, run by make -C docs test.

docs.title: docs-version.sh REF
docs.text:
Prints the version X.Y of a release tag vX.Y.Z or of a branch docs/X.Y. REF may carry a refs/tags/ or refs/heads/ prefix. Anything else prints not a release tag vX.Y.Z or a docs/X.Y branch: REF on stderr and exits 1.

$ devenv/scripts/docs-version.sh refs/tags/v0.10.2
0.10

docs.title: docs-guard.sh BRANCH [TAG]
docs.text: Checks HEAD as the tip of BRANCH, docs/X.Y with an optional refs/heads/ prefix, against TAG, by default the newest vX.Y.Z tag of that minor. See Docs-only guard. Prints the tag and exits 0, or prints a message on stderr and exits 1.

docs.title: docs-publish.sh REF
docs.text:
Publishes the current checkout as version X.Y of REF, a release tag or a docs/X.Y branch, with an optional refs/ prefix, to origin's gh-pages. Run from the repository root, with mike installed and a git committer configured.

  1. Maps REF to its version with docs-version.sh. For a docs/ branch, runs docs-guard.sh and takes the title from the tag it prints; for a tag, the title is the tag. The leading v is dropped.
  2. Fetches gh-pages from origin into the local gh-pages branch, if it exists there.
  3. Applies the latest rule: mike deploy -F mkdocs.mike.yml --title <title> --update-aliases X.Y latest and mike set-default -F mkdocs.mike.yml latest, or only mike deploy -F mkdocs.mike.yml --title <title> X.Y.
  4. Writes 404.html and .nojekyll to the root of gh-pages, in a separate commit, Root files: 404 redirect to latest, .nojekyll, only if they changed.
  5. Pushes gh-pages to origin.

It exits non-zero, before anything is pushed, if REF is not a release tag or a docs branch, or if the guard refuses.

docs.title: docs-links.sh [ROOT]
docs.text: Runs the link check on the repository at ROOT, by default the one the script is in. Exits 0 when every pinned link is right or site_url is unset, 1 otherwise.

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text:
wgpathd reports failures as uppercase codes, defined in src/wgpathd/errors.uc. In logs a code appears as CODE (detail), or CODE alone when there is no text detail. A detail can itself contain a nested code, as in INTERFACE_MISSING (wg_mesh: WG_PARSE_FAILED (no interface wg_mesh)).

Where each code is logged is listed in Log messages.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
These stop startup, fail the config check that service wgpathd start and reload run, and make a reload keep the running configuration. service wgpathd check shows them as readable FAIL config: lines instead; see Service commands.

Code Detail Trigger CONFIG_INVALID_ROLE the configured role, or unset role is not spoke or hub. CONFIG_MISSING_OPTION option name A required option for the role is missing or empty. CONFIG_INVALID_OPTION the option's name, then what it must be: <name> must be … An option has a value it cannot take: an interface option that is not a name of letters, digits and _, a discovery that is not an http:// URL, a serve_addr that is not an address the hub can listen on, a serve_port that is not a decimal port number, or a timing parameter out of its bounds or, on a spoke, in conflict with another. INTERFACE_MISSING interface name From configuration: an interface option names no network section of type interface. At startup: the interface is not in the wireguard status reply; the detail is <iface>: <cause>.

docs.title: ubus config object
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger CHECK_INVALID_CANDIDATE what is wrong with the candidate A candidate passed to ubus call wgpathd.config check does not follow its rules. It is returned as { "error": "CHECK_INVALID_CANDIDATE", "message": "<detail>" } and nothing is checked; see ubus config check. PEERS_INVALID_IFACE iface must name a WireGuard interface of /etc/config/network The iface passed to ubus call wgpathd.config peers is not the name of an interface section with proto 'wireguard'. It is returned as { "error": "PEERS_INVALID_IFACE", "message": "<detail>" } and no peer is read; see ubus config check.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger MIGRATE_FAILED cannot add a peer to /etc/config/wgpathd: <uci error>, cannot set <option> in /etc/config/wgpathd: <uci error>, cannot write /etc/config/wgpathd: <uci error>, cannot remove <option> from network section <section>: <uci error>, cannot write /etc/config/network: <uci error> The move of peer settings out of /etc/config/network failed; /etc/config/network is left as it was. See How to upgrade from a release that kept peer settings in the network configuration.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
These make a spoke's discovery fetch fail. The spoke keeps its previous map.

Code Detail Trigger DISCOVERY_FETCH_FAILED invalid url <url> (shown as described in Log messages), cannot connect, uclient error <n>, timeout, response too large, HTTP <status> The HTTP fetch did not produce a 200 response of at most 65536 bytes within 5 seconds. DISCOVERY_INVALID_JSON — The body is not a JSON object. DISCOVERY_INVALID_PEERS too many peers, invalid public key, or the key of the bad entry The object has more than 64 entries, a key that is not a public key, or an invalid entry. CACHE_SAVE_FAILED <cache path>: <cause>, where the cause is a system error, <dir> is not a directory, <dir> is not owned by root, <dir> is writable by others or <path>.tmp is a symbolic link A valid payload could not be written to the discovery cache. The payload is used all the same.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger EXEC_TIMEOUT the command name, wg wg set did not exit within 2 seconds. It appears inside WG_COMMAND_FAILED.

docs.title: Probes
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger PROBE_SEND_FAILED <host>: <socket error>, raw socket: <socket error>, raw socket on <device>: <socket error>, no random bytes, or <host>: not an IP address A probe could not be sent: the raw socket could not be opened or bound to mesh_iface, /dev/urandom gave no bytes for the probe's nonce, or the kernel refused the packet, for example with Message too large when a full-size tunnel probe does not fit the route. The probe counts as unanswered.

docs.title: WireGuard
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger WG_COMMAND_FAILED exit <code>, or a nested EXEC_TIMEOUT wg set <iface> peer <key> endpoint <addr> [peer <key> endpoint <addr> ...], one command for every peer, failed. WG_PARSE_FAILED no interface <iface>, no peer table, invalid peer entry The ubus call wireguard status reply does not contain the interface, has no peer table for it, or has a peer entry with a malformed key or handshake time.

docs.title: Routing and links
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger ROUTE_LOOKUP_FAILED <host>: <error> The route lookup for a peer's relay host failed. The peer stays unmanaged and is rechecked every cycle. service wgpathd check also shows it in a warning when the lookup for the discovery host fails. A failed lookup for a direct candidate is not reported: the candidate is kept, and its probes fail on their own. LINK_LOOKUP_FAILED <iface>: <error> The MTU of mesh_iface could not be read. No tunnel probe is sent that cycle.

docs.title: ubus
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger UBUS_CONNECT_FAILED — The daemon could not connect to ubus at startup; every ubus operation then fails with this code. service wgpathd status reports it as wgpathd: cannot read status: UBUS_CONNECT_FAILED, and service wgpathd check skips the interfaces. UBUS_CALL_FAILED <object> <method>: status <n> for wireguard status, or the ubus error text A ubus call failed: the wireguard status read or the watchdog ping. UBUS_PUBLISH_FAILED ubus error text The wgpathd ubus object could not be registered, for example because another instance holds it. Stops startup.

docs.title: Publisher
docs.text: Code Detail Trigger PUBLISHER_LISTEN_FAILED <addr>:<port>: <socket error> The hub could not listen on serve_addr:serve_port. Stops startup.

docs.title: Files and Dependencies
docs.text: The package is wgpathd, version 0.1.0, release 8, architecture all, license MIT. It is built as wgpathd-0.1.0-r8.apk.

docs.title: Installed files
docs.text:
Path Mode Description /usr/libexec/wgpathd/daemon.uc 0755 The daemon, run by procd. /usr/libexec/wgpathd/status.uc 0755 Prints the running daemon's status as text, for service wgpathd status. /usr/libexec/wgpathd/check.uc 0755 The validator behind service wgpathd check; with --config, the check that start and reload run. /usr/libexec/wgpathd/migrate.uc 0755 Moves the peer settings of releases up to 4 out of /etc/config/network, for service wgpathd migrate and the uci-defaults script below. /etc/uci-defaults/50-wgpathd-peers 0755 Runs migrate.uc once; see below. /usr/share/ucode/wgpathd/*.uc 0644 The ucode modules, imported as wgpathd.<module>. /usr/share/ucode/wgpathd/components/*.uc 0644 I/O components: command runner, ICMP prober, HTTP client, clock. /etc/config/wgpathd 0600 UCI configuration; a conffile, kept on upgrade. See UCI configuration. /etc/init.d/wgpathd 0755 procd init script. See below. /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/wgpathd.uc 0644 rpcd plugin serving the wgpathd.config ubus object. See ubus config check.

Nothing is installed on the PATH, and no firewall rule: the operator adds what wgpathd needs, see Firewall rules. The scripts in /usr/libexec/wgpathd/ are ucode scripts, meant to be run through the init script; see Service commands.

docs.title: Runtime files
docs.text:
Path Description /var/run/wgpathd/cache.json Spoke only. The last valid discovery payload, as JSON. Written through cache.json.tmp and a rename after each successful fetch; read and re-validated at startup. On tmpfs, so it survives a restart of the daemon but not a reboot. An unreadable or invalid file is treated as empty. The directory is set to mode 0700 and the file to 0600, whatever the umask. wgpathd neither writes nor reads the cache when /var/run/wgpathd is not a directory owned by root, or others may write to it. It does not read a cache.json that is not a regular file, and does not write when cache.json.tmp is a symbolic link; the temporary file is always created anew.

The daemon writes no other files, and never writes /etc/config. Only the migration does, as described below.

docs.title: /etc/init.d/wgpathd
docs.text:
A procd service with START=95 and STOP=10. When option enabled is on and the configuration passes check.uc --config, it runs one instance, named wgpathd, with:

Setting Value Effect command /usr/libexec/wgpathd/daemon.uc Runs the daemon. respawn 3600 5 0 Restarts the daemon 5 seconds after it exits, with no retry limit. watchdog 1 30 Passive watchdog: procd restarts the instance if it has not been pinged for 30 seconds. The daemon pings at the end of every cycle. stderr 1 Standard error goes to the system log, under daemon.uc[<PID>]. The daemon's messages go to syslog directly, so this only catches an uncaught exception. Trigger Effect config.change for wgpathd reload config.change for network reload

The script adds the check and migrate commands and replaces reload and status. What each command does is in Service commands.

docs.title: /etc/uci-defaults/50-wgpathd-peers
docs.text:
A uci-defaults script: OpenWrt runs it once, then deletes it. It runs /usr/libexec/wgpathd/migrate.uc, which moves the options wgpathd_relay and wgpathd_tunnel of every wireguard_* section in /etc/config/network into the peer section with that section's public_key in /etc/config/wgpathd, as relay and tunnel:

  • It adds a peer section only for a key that has none, and never replaces a value the section already holds. A value it does not take is logged, and dropped from network all the same.
  • It commits /etc/config/wgpathd first, and only then deletes the two options from /etc/config/network and commits it. It writes no copy of either file.
  • A section without a valid public_key cannot be keyed: its options stay, and are logged.
  • With nothing to move it changes nothing and exits 0.
  • When a step fails, /etc/config/network is left as it was and the script exits non-zero, so OpenWrt keeps it and runs it again at the next boot.

It runs on a first install and on every upgrade, from the package's post-install script (below), and at boot while it is still there. Its log lines start with migrate:; see Log messages. service wgpathd migrate runs the same program by hand. How to upgrade from a release that kept peer settings in the network configuration shows how to check it.

docs.title: Package scripts
docs.text:
Script Effect post-install (install and upgrade) OpenWrt's default first: run the package's uci-defaults script, which moves peer settings left in /etc/config/network; on a first install, enable the service; on both, run start, which does nothing while enabled is 0 or the daemon is already running. Then /etc/init.d/rpcd reload; /etc/init.d/firewall reload when rules with a wgpathd: comment are loaded, which only a release up to 5 left, whose include the upgrade has just removed; and on an upgrade, restart the daemon if it is running so the new code takes over. The migration has run by then, so the restarted daemon reads the moved settings. post-remove /etc/init.d/rpcd reload.

The rpcd reload makes rpcd load the wgpathd.config plugin, or drop it after removal, and pick up new module code after an upgrade. rpcd re-executes itself and keeps its sessions, so LuCI users stay logged in.

The reloads and the restart are skipped when the package is installed into a firmware image rather than on a running router.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Package Used for ucode The interpreter ucode-mod-uloop Event loop, timers, the wg set process ucode-mod-fs Discovery cache, random bytes for the probes (/dev/urandom) ucode-mod-ubus wireguard status, status object, watchdog ping ucode-mod-uci Configuration ucode-mod-log syslog ucode-mod-socket Spoke probes (raw ICMP and ICMPv6 sockets), hub discovery listener ucode-mod-rtnl Relay route lookup, the MTU of mesh_iface ucode-mod-uclient Spoke discovery fetch rpcd-mod-wireguard The wireguard status ubus method rpcd-mod-ucode Runs the wgpathd.config plugin inside rpcd wireguard-tools wg set kmod-wireguard WireGuard in the kernel

The probes need no command: the daemon sends them itself on raw sockets, which needs root, as procd runs it.

docs.title: luci-app-wgpathd
docs.text: The LuCI pages for wgpathd are a second package, luci-app-wgpathd, built from the same source with the same version and release, architecture all, license MIT: luci-app-wgpathd-0.1.0-r8.apk. It is optional; the daemon does not need it.

docs.title: Installed files
docs.text: Path Mode Description /www/luci-static/resources/view/wgpathd/status.js 0644 The Status → Mesh paths page. /www/luci-static/resources/view/wgpathd/settings.js 0644 The Network → Mesh paths page. /www/luci-static/resources/wgpathd.js 0644 Shared by the pages and the Overview section ('require wgpathd'): the status call, the path strip, and the words for states, times and reasons. /www/luci-static/resources/view/status/include/70_wgpathd.js 0644 The Mesh paths section of Status → Overview. Hidden while the service is not running, on a hub, and when no peer is steered. /usr/share/luci/menu.d/luci-app-wgpathd.json 0644 The two menu entries, admin/status/wgpathd and admin/network/wgpathd. Each is shown only to a session granted the luci-app-wgpathd ACL, and only while /etc/config/wgpathd exists. /usr/share/rpcd/acl.d/luci-app-wgpathd.json 0644 The luci-app-wgpathd ACL; see below.

docs.title: ACL
docs.text:
Access Grants read ubus wgpathd status; ubus wgpathd.config check, peers and schema; UCI wgpathd write UCI wgpathd

It grants nothing of /etc/config/network, which holds every WireGuard private key of the router, nor of /etc/config/firewall, which the configuration check reads inside rpcd. The pages name the peers through the peers method, which returns each peer's section name, public key and description and nothing else, and a peer's settings are peer sections of /etc/config/wgpathd.

The pages also read the router's host name and time zone from UCI system, which the luci-base ACL already grants: the name labels this router in the path strip, and the time zone sets the clock times of recent changes, as in the system log. Without it they show "This router" and UTC.

docs.title: Package scripts
docs.text:
Script Effect post-install (install and upgrade) OpenWrt's default first, then the same as LuCI's own applications: delete LuCI's menu and module caches (/tmp/luci-indexcache.*, /tmp/luci-modulecache/) so the new menu entries appear, and /etc/init.d/rpcd reload so rpcd reads the new ACL. post-remove The same cache deletion and rpcd reload.

Both are skipped when the package is installed into a firmware image rather than on a running router.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Package Used for luci-base LuCI itself, and read access to UCI system wgpathd, exactly the same version and release (wgpathd=0.1.0-r8) The ubus objects and the configuration the pages read and write. apk refuses to install the app next to any other wgpathd release, and keeps the daemon while the app is installed.

docs.title: Firewall Rules
docs.text: The package ships no firewall rules and never changes the firewall. The operator adds the rules below to /etc/config/firewall, as How to open the firewall for wgpathd shows, and service wgpathd check looks for them.

docs.title: What each role needs
docs.text:
Role Traffic Arrives on Rule Spoke ICMP echo request to the spoke's address on mesh_iface; ICMPv6 when that address is IPv6 The zone of mesh_iface Tunnel probe Spoke UDP to the listen_port of mesh_iface The zone of hub_iface Relayed packets Spoke ICMPv6 echo request to the spoke's public IPv6 address The wan zone Underlay probe: OpenWrt's Allow-ICMPv6-Input Hub TCP to serve_port on serve_addr The zone of the WireGuard interface that holds serve_addr Peer list

Nothing else is needed for wgpathd. Answers to what a node sends, the echo replies to its probes and the reply to its peer list request, are accepted as part of an established connection. What WireGuard itself needs, the listen ports from WAN and forwarding between the hub's wg_hub peers, is part of the substrate: see How to prepare the WireGuard substrate.

A zone whose input policy is ACCEPT already accepts all of it.

docs.title: Tunnel probe
docs.text:
config rule
    option name 'Allow-wgpathd-tunnel-probe'
    option src 'vpn'
    option proto 'icmp'
    option icmp_type 'echo-request'
    option family 'ipv4'
    option target 'ACCEPT'

Every cycle, each other spoke pings this spoke's tunnel address through wg_mesh: to test a direct path, and then to keep checking it. Without an answer, no trial succeeds and a peer on a direct path falls back to the relay. src is the zone of mesh_iface. The probe goes to the address the other spokes have as this spoke's tunnel; family is that address's, and is left out when mesh_iface has addresses of both families.

docs.title: Relayed packets
docs.text:
config rule
    option name 'Allow-wgpathd-relay'
    option src 'vpn'
    option proto 'udp'
    option dest_port '51820'
    option target 'ACCEPT'

When a pair uses the relay, the other spoke sends its wg_mesh packets to this spoke's relay endpoint, its transit address and wg_mesh listen port. The hub forwards them, and they arrive out of hub_iface, addressed to that port. Without the rule the relay works only in the direction this spoke opened first. src is the zone of hub_iface, and dest_port the listen_port of mesh_iface in /etc/config/network.

docs.title: Underlay probe
docs.text: Each other spoke pings this spoke's public IPv6 address from the internet, for evidence that a direct path may work. OpenWrt's default configuration accepts this with its rule Allow-ICMPv6-Input on wan, limited to 1000 packets a second, and wgpathd needs no rule of its own. A spoke that does not answer gets no direct path from the others' evidence; the others may still reach it after it contacts them.

docs.title: Peer list
docs.text:
config rule
    option name 'Allow-wgpathd-discovery'
    option src 'vpn'
    option proto 'tcp'
    option dest_port '7780'
    option target 'ACCEPT'

The spokes fetch the peer list from the hub's serve_addr and serve_port, through the hub tunnel. src is the zone of the WireGuard interface that holds serve_addr, and dest_port is serve_port. Accepting the port from another zone opens the list to whatever that zone reaches.

docs.title: What the check confirms
docs.text:
On a live system, service wgpathd check and the ubus config check read /etc/config/firewall and, for each traffic of the role, say whether it is accepted (ok), not accepted (warn, with the rule to add) or cannot be confirmed (warn). check.uc --config, which start and reload run, does not look at the firewall. Without /etc/config/firewall the check says skip firewall: no /etc/config/firewall, not checked. The findings are listed in Service commands.

It reads the configuration the way fw4 does:

  • The zone of an interface is the first enabled zone that takes it: its network lists the interface, or its device names the interface's device. netifd names a WireGuard interface's device after the interface, so a zone with list device 'wg_hub' takes the interface wg_hub. A device may end in + to match every device that starts with the rest, wg+ for instance, as fw4 reads it. A zone with a name fw4 would refuse is skipped.
  • The rules that apply are enabled rule sections without dest: first those with src '*', then those of the zone, in the order of the file. The first rule whose target is ACCEPT, REJECT or DROP and that covers the traffic decides. Without one, the zone's input decides, or the input of defaults when the zone has none. An interface in no zone gets only the src '*' rules and the default input.
  • A rule covers the traffic when its family, or its zone's when it has none, includes the traffic's; its proto names the protocol (unset means TCP and UDP; all, tcpudp, protocol numbers, and icmp for ICMPv6 too unless the family says otherwise); its dest_port includes the port (a port, a range a-b or a:b, or a list; unset is every port); and its icmp_type includes an echo request (echo-request, ping, 8 or 8/0, 128 for ICMPv6; unset is every type). Lists may be UCI lists or words in one option. A limit does not stop a rule from accepting.

It could not confirm a traffic, rather than call it missing, when:

  • a rule that may decide it has options the check does not follow: src_ip, src_mac, src_port, dest_ip, device, ipset, helper, mark, dscp, a time restriction or extra, or an inverted (!) or unreadable protocol or port, or it is an ICMP rule for both families that names only other types;
  • the zone has extra_src or extra, or its family excludes the traffic's;
  • a zone that may take the traffic in a way the check does not follow comes before the interface's zone, or no zone takes the interface and one may: a zone with a subnet (unless its device list leaves the interface out), an inverted (!) network or device, a device of + alone or with a *; for the underlay probe, which comes from the wan zone rather than an interface, any zone with a device or subnet before wan;
  • the firewall has custom nftables rules: an enabled include section, or a file with anything but comments in /etc/nftables.d/*.nft, /usr/share/nftables.d/ruleset-*/, /usr/share/nftables.d/table-*/ or /usr/share/nftables.d/chain-*/input*/;
  • mesh_iface has no listen_port, so the relay port is not known;
  • there is no zone named wan, for the underlay probe.

It does not see rules that other services add at runtime through procd, nor tables other than fw4's. Those cannot accept what fw4 rejects, but they can drop what it accepts.

Every firewall finding is a warning, never FAIL: a custom firewall may accept the traffic in ways the check cannot see, so neither the service nor LuCI's Save & Apply refuses a configuration over it. A warning names the wgpathd option the traffic follows from, mesh_iface, hub_iface or serve_port, and, when there is a zone to name and a port, carries the rule to add as uci commands and as a section of /etc/config/firewall. The rule to add for an interface in no zone is to put it in one.

docs.title: Releases up to 5
docs.text:
Releases up to 5 installed an fw4 include, /usr/share/nftables.d/chain-pre/input/wgpathd.nft, which put four accepts at the top of the input chain, before any zone rule: ICMPv6 echo requests from anywhere, without a rate limit, and ICMP echo requests, TCP 7780 and UDP 51820 from every WireGuard interface. They bypassed the operator's zone policy, and the first let a flood from the internet keep the daemon busy.

An upgrade removes the file, and the package's post-install script reloads the firewall once while rules with a wgpathd: comment are still loaded, so they leave the running ruleset too. Add the rules above before upgrading such a node: from the reload on, a zone that rejects input rejects wgpathd's traffic until they are there.

docs.title: Log Messages
docs.text:
wgpathd logs to syslog with the identifier wgpathd, its PID, and facility daemon.

logread -e wgpathd

A line looks like this:

Sun Sep 27 10:15:03 2026 daemon.notice wgpathd[2481]: peer spoke_b (SpokeBme): transition RELAY -> TRIALING reason=trial_start endpoint=[2001:db8:b::20]:51820

When the daemon runs in the foreground with standard error on a terminal, or with WGPATHD_STDERR=1 in its environment, each message is also written to standard error, prefixed by its level, as in notice: started role=hub. Under procd standard error is not a terminal, so nothing is logged twice.

An uncaught exception is not a wgpathd message: procd forwards the daemon's standard error to syslog under the identifier daemon.uc[<PID>], so logread -e wgpathd does not show it. Use logread -e daemon.uc to find one.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
Level syslog priority Shown by logread as Used for err LOG_ERR daemon.err The daemon cannot run, or refuses a new configuration. warning LOG_WARNING daemon.warn A problem that needs attention: an outage, or a peer left unmanaged by a configuration error. notice LOG_NOTICE daemon.notice An event an operator wants to see: a path change, a recovery, start, stop and reload. info LOG_INFO daemon.info Routine detail.

wgpathd logs nothing at debug.

docs.title: Message grammar
docs.text:
The format of every message is stable, so it can be matched by scripts:

[<subject>: ]<event>[ key=value ...]
  • A line about a peer has the subject peer <section> (<key prefix>): the peer's UCI section in /etc/config/network and the first 8 characters of its public key. A peer with no valid public key has the subject peer <section>.
  • Keys and values contain no spaces, except the value of the last key, which runs to the end of the line (such as reason=relay routes into wg_mesh).
  • An outage is reported as a pair: [<subject>: ]<what> failed: <CODE> (<detail>) when it starts, and [<subject>: ]<what> recovered when it ends. The failed line is not repeated while the outage lasts, even if the code or detail changes.

In the tables below, <CODE> (<detail>) is an error code with its detail. When a failure has no text detail, only the code appears. <peer> stands for the peer subject.

docs.title: Startup and exit
docs.text:
Level Message Meaning err invalid configuration: <CODE> (<detail>) /etc/config/wgpathd failed validation. The daemon exits with status 1. Under the init script this is normally caught before the daemon starts; see Init script. See UCI configuration. err startup failed: <CODE> (<detail>) The interface was not in wireguard status, the ubus object could not be published, or the hub listener could not bind. The daemon exits with status 1, and procd starts it again after 5 seconds. warning network section <section>: ignoring <options>, left over from an earlier version; run service wgpathd migrate The section of /etc/config/network still has wgpathd_relay, wgpathd_tunnel or both (<options>, joined by and), which this release does not read. Logged once per section at startup, in both roles, not on reload. See How to upgrade from a release that kept peer settings in the network configuration. warning unknown mode, running in observe mode value=<mode> The spoke's mode is neither steer nor observe. Logged at startup and on every reload. info discovery cache: loaded peers=<n> A spoke started with <n> peers from the discovery cache in /var/run/wgpathd/cache.json. info discovery cache: none usable A spoke started without a discovery cache, or with one that failed validation. notice started role=spoke mode=<mode> managed=<n> unmanaged=<n> A spoke completed startup; the first cycle follows. unmanaged counts peers waiting on a relay route too. notice started role=hub A hub completed startup. notice stopped The daemon left its loop and exits with status 0: procd stopped it (service wgpathd stop or restart), or a reload needs a new process. notice stopped code=<n> The daemon left its loop and exits with status <n>, as after startup failed:.

Typical startup failures:

invalid configuration: CONFIG_INVALID_ROLE (unset)
invalid configuration: CONFIG_MISSING_OPTION (discovery)
invalid configuration: INTERFACE_MISSING (wg_mesh)
invalid configuration: CONFIG_INVALID_OPTION (n_up must be a whole number from 1 to 100)
startup failed: INTERFACE_MISSING (wg_mesh: WG_PARSE_FAILED (no interface wg_mesh))
startup failed: PUBLISHER_LISTEN_FAILED (10.10.0.1:7780: bind(): Address not available)

invalid configuration: INTERFACE_MISSING means no UCI interface section has that name. startup failed: INTERFACE_MISSING means the UCI section exists but the kernel interface is not in the wireguard status reply, typically because it is down.

docs.title: Init script
docs.text:
service wgpathd start and service wgpathd reload run the config check first. When it fails, the init script logs through logger with the tag wgpathd (no PID) at daemon.err: each line of the check report, then one of:

Level Message Meaning err FAIL config: <reason> The failed check. The reasons are listed in Service commands. err invalid configuration, not starting start created no instance. err invalid configuration, keeping the running one reload did not signal the daemon; it keeps its configuration.

The same lines go to standard error of the service command.

docs.title: Reload
docs.text:
Level Message Meaning notice configuration reloaded peers_kept=<n> added=<n> removed=<n> A spoke applied a reload. Kept peers had the same key, relay and tunnel address; a changed peer counts as removed and added. mode=<mode> is appended when the mode changed. notice configuration reloaded A hub applied a reload. Only cycle applies live on a hub; its other options need a new process. info <peer>: added A reload added this managed peer. It starts in RELAY. info <peer>: changed A reload changed this peer's relay or tunnel address. It starts again in RELAY. info <peer>: removed A reload removed this peer from steering. notice reload: exiting for procd to start afresh changed=<option> The reload changes an option that needs a new process. The daemon exits with status 0 and procd starts it again after 5 seconds. err reload: invalid configuration, keeping the running one: <CODE> (<detail>) The configuration read on SIGHUP is invalid. Nothing changes.

What a reload applies is listed in Service commands.

docs.title: Unmanaged peers (spoke)
docs.text: Level Message Meaning warning <peer>: unmanaged reason=<reason> A mesh peer will not be steered: invalid public_key, not configured, fixed endpoint, configured more than once, missing relay, invalid relay, missing tunnel, invalid tunnel, or relay routes into <mesh_iface>. Logged once per peer at startup, when a reload adds or changes the peer, and when a waiting peer's relay route later resolves into mesh_iface. The hub peer, which has a fixed endpoint and no peer section, is logged with fixed endpoint. See Managed and unmanaged peers. info <peer>: unmanaged reason=relay route lookup failed: <CODE> (<detail>) The route lookup for the peer's relay host failed, typically because wg_hub is not up yet. It is retried every cycle. notice <peer>: relay route found, now managed A peer whose relay route lookup had failed, or that a reload guarded again, now has a route outside mesh_iface and is steered from now on.

docs.title: Path changes (spoke)
docs.text:
Level Message Meaning notice <peer>: transition <from> -> <to> reason=<reason>[ failed_probes=<n>][ backoff=<s>s] endpoint=<endpoint> A state transition. endpoint is the endpoint wgpathd sets for the new state. demoted adds failed_probes (the m_down probes in a row that were lost or answered over the relay) and backoff; trial_timeout adds backoff. The reasons are listed below. notice <peer>: roamed endpoint=<endpoint> In DIRECT, the peer's kernel endpoint moved to a new direct address, which is now the target. notice <peer>: ready, steer would trial endpoint=<endpoint> Observe mode only: the peer has earned n_up cycles of direct evidence, or saw an authenticated roam this cycle. endpoint is the endpoint a trial would take: the roam's source if one was seen, else the discovered endpoint. In steer mode it would start a trial now. Logged once, until no longer ready. info <peer>: no longer ready Observe mode only: the peer is not ready and has had no direct evidence for more than n_up cycles in a row. A roam makes a peer ready for its cycle alone, so the line waits out the cycles between roams instead of following each one. warning <peer>: candidate refused endpoint=<endpoint> reason=<reason> The peer's candidate from discovery is not taken, for one of the reasons in Discovery HTTP API: own address, relay address, tunnel address or routes into <iface>. Logged when the refusal starts or its reason changes. Meanwhile the candidate is neither probed nor trialed. notice <peer>: candidate no longer refused The refused candidate is taken again, or discovery no longer offers it. notice <peer>: direct address given up endpoint=<endpoint> failed_trials=<n> pause=<s>s Steer mode only: the trial toward endpoint timed out, the n-th in a row on that address, which reaches give_up_after. The underlay echo alone starts no trial toward it for pause (give_up_pause). Logged right after the trial_timeout transition. n is above give_up_after when the one trial after a pause or a roam failed as well. See Giving up an address. notice <peer>: direct address trials resumed reason=<reason> endpoint=<endpoint> Steer mode only: a trial starts although endpoint, the address given up, still was. Logged right before its trial_start transition. The reasons are listed below. Reason Transition trial_start RELAY → TRIALING trial_ok TRIALING → DIRECT, on a tunnel probe answered from the trial's target trial_timeout TRIALING → RELAY, no answer over the direct path within trial_window demoted DIRECT → RELAY after m_down failed probes observe_mode TRIALING or DIRECT → RELAY because the mode is not steer

The reasons of direct address trials resumed:

Reason Why trials resumed roam An authenticated roam: the peer's packets arrived directly. The trial takes the roam's source as its target. new_candidate Discovery offers another address for the peer, and it answers the underlay echo. The trial takes that address. pause_over give_up_pause has passed since the address was given up. The trial takes the given-up address once more.

For example:

peer spoke_b (SpokeBme): transition RELAY -> TRIALING reason=trial_start endpoint=[2001:db8:b::20]:51820
peer spoke_b (SpokeBme): transition TRIALING -> DIRECT reason=trial_ok endpoint=[2001:db8:b::20]:51820
peer spoke_b (SpokeBme): roamed endpoint=[2001:db8:b::21]:51820
peer spoke_b (SpokeBme): transition DIRECT -> RELAY reason=demoted failed_probes=2 backoff=60s endpoint=10.10.0.12:51820

An address that answers ping but not WireGuard, given up at the third timeout and tried once more when the pause is over:

peer spoke_c (SpokeCme): transition TRIALING -> RELAY reason=trial_timeout backoff=120s endpoint=10.10.0.13:51820
peer spoke_c (SpokeCme): direct address given up endpoint=[2001:db8:c::30]:51820 failed_trials=3 pause=21600s
peer spoke_c (SpokeCme): direct address trials resumed reason=pause_over endpoint=[2001:db8:c::30]:51820
peer spoke_c (SpokeCme): transition RELAY -> TRIALING reason=trial_start endpoint=[2001:db8:c::30]:51820
peer spoke_c (SpokeCme): transition TRIALING -> RELAY reason=trial_timeout backoff=240s endpoint=10.10.0.13:51820
peer spoke_c (SpokeCme): direct address given up endpoint=[2001:db8:c::30]:51820 failed_trials=4 pause=21600s

docs.title: Cycle problems
docs.text:
Level Message Role Meaning warning reading <iface> failed: <CODE> (<detail>) both ubus call wireguard status failed or did not contain the interface. A spoke decides nothing while this lasts; a hub keeps its last snapshot. notice reading <iface> recovered both The first successful read after a failure. warning <peer>: absent from <mesh_iface>, skipped spoke A managed peer is not in the kernel's peer table. Logged once each time it disappears; the peer is skipped until it returns. notice <peer>: back in <mesh_iface> spoke The absent peer is in the kernel's peer table again and is steered from this cycle. warning setting endpoints on <mesh_iface> failed: WG_COMMAND_FAILED (<detail>) spoke The cycle's wg set, which sets every peer's endpoint in one command, failed. The detail is exit <code>, or EXEC_TIMEOUT (wg) if it took more than 2 seconds. No tunnel probe is sent while it fails. notice setting endpoints on <mesh_iface> recovered spoke The first successful wg set after a failure. warning reading the MTU of <mesh_iface> failed: LINK_LOOKUP_FAILED (<detail>) spoke The MTU that sizes the tunnel probes could not be read. No tunnel probe is sent while it fails. notice reading the MTU of <mesh_iface> recovered spoke The first successful MTU read after a failure. warning sending probes failed: PROBE_SEND_FAILED (<detail>) spoke At least one probe of a cycle could not be sent; the detail is the first such failure. The probe counts as unanswered. notice sending probes recovered spoke The first cycle whose probes could all be sent, after a failure. warning discovery failed: <CODE> (<detail>) spoke A discovery fetch failed. See Discovery HTTP API. notice discovery recovered spoke The first successful fetch after a failure. warning saving the discovery cache failed: CACHE_SAVE_FAILED (/var/run/wgpathd/cache.json: <cause>) spoke A valid payload was received but the cache file could not be written; the causes are listed in Error codes. The payload is still used. notice saving the discovery cache recovered spoke The first successful cache write after a failure. warning watchdog ping failed: <CODE> (<detail>) both The ubus call service watchdog at the end of a cycle failed. notice watchdog ping recovered both The first successful watchdog ping after a failure.

Each failed: line in this table marks the start of an outage; the matching recovered line marks its end.

watchdog ping failed without a recovery usually means procd does not know the service wgpathd, for example when the daemon was started by hand or in a container without procd.

A URL in a message shows the scheme, host, port and path only: never the user:password@ part, the query or the fragment. A value that does not read as scheme://host[:port] shows as (unreadable url).

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
/usr/libexec/wgpathd/migrate.uc, run by the uci-defaults script /etc/uci-defaults/50-wgpathd-peers after an install or upgrade and by service wgpathd migrate, logs through the same syslog identifier, wgpathd, each message starting with migrate:. It logs nothing when there is nothing to move.

logread -e 'migrate:'
Level Message Meaning notice migrate: moved the settings of <n> peer(s) from /etc/config/network to /etc/config/wgpathd Both files are committed: the peer sections hold the settings, and the options are gone from network. warning migrate: network section <section>: kept <option> '<value>' of /etc/config/wgpathd, dropped <legacy option> '<value>' The peer's peer section already had a different relay or tunnel. That value is kept; the one from network is removed with the rest. warning migrate: network section <section> has no valid public_key, its options stay The section cannot be keyed, so its options are not moved. service wgpathd check keeps warning about them. err migrate: failed, /etc/config/network left as it was: MIGRATE_FAILED (<detail>) A step failed; the details are listed in Error codes. Settings already committed to /etc/config/wgpathd stay, and a later run finishes the job. Run from the uci-defaults script, it runs again at the next boot.

docs.title: Make Targets
docs.text: All targets run in Docker. Nothing is installed on the host.

docs.title: Root Makefile
docs.text:
Target Description test Run the unit and integration suites. unit Run the unit suite only. integration Run the integration suite only. watch Run all tests, then re-run whenever a file under src/, test/ or files/ changes. lint Compile-check every ucode file, sh -n every shell script, parse every JSON file under luci/ with ucode and every LuCI script under luci/ with quickjs (as the function body LuCI compiles it into), fail on innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write or %s in a .format() template in those scripts (devenv/scripts/luci-dom-lint.sh, which lint first proves still catches each), and check the pinned documentation links with devenv/scripts/docs-links.sh (see Link check). Then check that luci/po/templates/wgpathd.pot is what pot would write, and that the scanner gave no warning. shell Open a throwaway shell in the development image. image Rebuild the development image, pulling the base image again. package Build bin/wgpathd-<version>-r<release>.apk and bin/luci-app-wgpathd-<version>-r<release>.apk in the OpenWrt SDK. package-check Run package, then install both packages offline in an OpenWrt rootfs container that already carries their dependencies (no network, NET_ADMIN in its own empty namespace) and check files, modes, package scripts, clean failure paths, that the package ships no firewall rules and that an upgrade from a release with the fw4 include unloads its rules, the app's pin to the daemon's version, that the app's JSON and views parse and its scripts clear LuCI's caches, and removal. pot Write luci/po/templates/wgpathd.pot, the translation template of luci-app-wgpathd, with openwrt/luci's build/i18n-scan.pl, run over luci/ laid out as applications/luci-app-wgpathd of the luci tree. The scanner is the one of the luci commit the OpenWrt 25.12.5 SDK pins (devenv/services/i18n/Dockerfile), in image wgpathd-i18n:<hash> (Alpine with perl and gettext), which runs without network. Fails, and writes nothing, when the scanner warns. browser Run package, then the Playwright tests in test/browser/ against the LuCI pages. LuCI (uhttpd on 127.0.0.1, rpcd with the package's own wgpathd.config plugin, ubusd, the built packages and a fake wgpathd ubus object answering test/fixtures/luci/, which also lays out the configurations of test/fixtures/luci/config/) runs in an OpenWrt rootfs container with --network none and no capabilities; Playwright runs in a second container joined to its network namespace with --network container:, so the two share only its loopback. Both are removed when the run ends. Images wgpathd-luci:<arch>-<version> and wgpathd-browser:<playwright version>. Screenshots and, on failure, the error context and the LuCI log in bin/browser/. e2e Run package, then the end-to-end failover scenarios against a hub and two spokes in OpenWrt containers (procd as PID 1, kernel WireGuard, fw4), compose project wgpathd-e2e, image wgpathd-e2e:<arch>-<version>. Refuses to start while another project's containers run, guards the host's Wi-Fi interface for the whole run, and always tears down. Results in bin/e2e/. lab-up Run package, then start the e2e topology as compose project wgpathd-lab (containers wgpathd-lab-hub, wgpathd-lab-spoke-a, wgpathd-lab-spoke-b) with the WireGuard substrate in place and wgpathd installed but disabled (shipped /etc/config/wgpathd, enabled '0') on every node. Returns once the hub has handshakes with both spokes on wg_hub and wg_mesh. The same host guards as e2e apply, and the watchdog keeps running in the background until lab-down. Guard logs in bin/lab/. lab-down Stop the lab's watchdog, tear the lab down and print the host report (sysctls, Wi-Fi interface, kernel log). Safe to run when the lab is not up. lab-shell Open a login shell on the lab node named by NODE. lab-fault Inject or clear a fault in the running lab, named by NAME: kill-direct drops the wg_mesh datagrams between the spokes (the e2e kill-direct fault: the hub leg, the relay and ICMPv6 stay up); relay-delay delays everything the hub sends by MS milliseconds (netem on the hub's eth0), which slows only the relay path, since the direct path never crosses the hub; restore clears every fault. docs Build the documentation site (same as make -C docs build). docs-mike Strict build with the versioned config (same as make -C docs build-mike). docs-test Test the docs publishing tooling (same as make -C docs test). docs-serve Serve the documentation with live reload (same as make -C docs serve).

test, unit, integration, watch, lint and shell run in the wgpathd-openwrt:<arch>-<version>-<hash> image, which is built on first use from devenv/services/openwrt/Dockerfile and rebuilt when that file or openwrt/wgpathd/Makefile changes. <hash> is taken from the Dockerfile and the daemon's dependencies, so two checkouts that need different images never overwrite each other's; images left behind by older hashes can be removed with docker image rm. The container has no network.
