docs.title: Timing Parameters
docs.text:
Each parameter can be overridden by an option of the same name in the main section of /etc/config/wgpathd, for example option n_up '3'. Values are in seconds unless noted. Each has bounds, described below. A running daemon picks up changed values on service wgpathd reload, from its next cycle.

Parameter Default Unit Used by Meaning cycle 3 s spoke, hub Pause between the end of one cycle and the start of the next. n_up 5 cycles spoke Consecutive cycles with direct evidence needed before a trial may start. An authenticated roam needs no streak. m_down 2 cycles spoke Consecutive failed tunnel probes in DIRECT that demote a peer to RELAY. A probe answered over the relay counts as failed. tunnel_timeout 1 s spoke How long the underlay probes and the tunnel probes wait for replies. trial_window 8 s spoke How long a trial may wait for a tunnel probe answer before it fails. backoff_min 30 s spoke Backoff after the first failed trial or demotion. backoff_max 900 s spoke Upper limit of the backoff. backoff_reset 600 s spoke Time a peer must stay in DIRECT before its backoff returns to zero. discovery_interval 60 s spoke Interval between regular discovery fetches. give_up_after 3 trials spoke Failed trials in a row on the same address after which the address is given up: the underlay echo alone no longer starts a trial toward it. give_up_pause 21600 s spoke How long an address stays given up before the echo may start one more trial toward it.

The hub uses only cycle, as the interval between snapshots of read_iface. It accepts and validates the other parameters but does not use them.

docs.title: Bounds
docs.text:
A value must be a decimal number within its bounds, both included; n_up, m_down and give_up_after must be whole numbers. A value outside them stops startup, fails service wgpathd check, and is refused on reload, which keeps the running values; the error is CONFIG_INVALID_OPTION with the detail <name> must be a number from <min> to <max>, or a whole number for the counts.

Parameter Minimum Maximum Why cycle 1 10 Every spoke cycle runs wg set and reads wireguard status: a shorter pause mostly starts processes. The maximum keeps the watchdog fed, see below. n_up 1 100 A count of cycles. m_down 1 100 A count of cycles. tunnel_timeout 0.1 5 Shorter than any real round trip it is meant to wait for, the probes would all count as lost. The maximum keeps the watchdog fed. trial_window 1 60 A trial sends the peer's traffic over an unproven path, so a failing one should not last longer than a minute. backoff_min, backoff_max, backoff_reset 1 86400 Up to a day. discovery_interval 5 86400 Every spoke fetches from the hub at this interval. give_up_after 1 100 A count of trials. give_up_pause 60 604800 From a minute to a week.

procd restarts the daemon when 30 seconds pass without a watchdog ping, and the daemon pings once per cycle, when the cycle completes. Between two pings a spoke waits cycle, up to tunnel_timeout for the underlay probes, up to 2 s for wg set, and up to tunnel_timeout for the tunnel probes: at the maxima 10 + 5 + 2 + 5 = 22 seconds, which leaves 8 for the wireguard status reads.

On a spoke, two combinations are refused as well, with the effective values, defaults included:

Rule Detail backoff_max ≥ backoff_min backoff_max must be at least backoff_min (<value>) trial_window > cycle + tunnel_timeout trial_window must be longer than cycle + tunnel_timeout (<sum>)

The first answer to a trial's probe is read a cycle, and a probe wait, after the trial starts, so a shorter window fails every trial. A hub is held to the bounds alone.

docs.title: Behavior details
docs.text:
cycle. The next cycle is scheduled cycle seconds after the current one completes. A spoke cycle completes when the wireguard status read, the underlay probes, the one wg set command, the tunnel probes and the endpoint reads that follow their answers have returned or timed out. The effective period is therefore cycle plus the time those take.

n_up. Evidence is counted only in RELAY. A cycle without evidence resets the count to zero. Every state change resets it. Counting continues during a backoff. A cycle in RELAY that sees an authenticated roam (the kernel endpoint moved to a direct address wgpathd did not set) is enough on its own: the trial toward the roamed address starts on that cycle, or on the first cycle after the backoff that still sees one.

m_down. In DIRECT, a tunnel probe that was not answered, timed out, or was not sent (for example because wg set failed) counts as failed. The probe fills the MTU of mesh_iface, so a path that loses full-size packets fails it even when small ones get through. Any answer resets the count, whichever path the kernel endpoint shows right after it. A trial is stricter: right after an answer, wgpathd reads the kernel endpoint, which the answer itself moved, and only an answer that came back from the trial's target commits it.

tunnel_timeout. wgpathd sends the probes itself, as ICMP echo requests, and waits exactly tunnel_timeout seconds for each reply, fractions included: 0.5 waits half a second. A reply that arrives later is ignored, even in a later cycle. The probes of one cycle go out together and wait together, so a cycle waits at most tunnel_timeout for the underlay probes of the peers in RELAY, and at most tunnel_timeout again, after wg set, for the tunnel probes of the peers trialing or in DIRECT.

trial_window. Measured from the cycle in which the trial started. The deadline is checked before the probe result: an answer that is read at or after the deadline is a timeout. The tunnel probe answer is read one cycle after it is sent. A good path answers the first probe and commits one cycle after the trial starts. A second probe is read two cycles after the start; while the path fails, each of those cycles lasts cycle plus about tunnel_timeout, so with the defaults the second answer arrives after the 8-second deadline and the trial times out on its first probe.

Backoff. A failed trial or a demotion sets the backoff to backoff_min if it was zero, otherwise to twice its value, capped at backoff_max. No trial starts until that many seconds have passed since the failure. While in DIRECT, once the peer has held DIRECT for backoff_reset, the backoff returns to zero. A demotion caused by switching to observe mode does not change the backoff.

give_up_after. Only a trial that times out counts, against its target: the endpoint, port included. A timeout on another target starts the count again at one, and a trial that commits clears it; a demotion from DIRECT does not count. At give_up_after timeouts in a row the address is given up, and the underlay echo alone starts no trial toward it. An authenticated roam still starts a trial at once, and so does echo evidence for another address from discovery. If the trial that follows is toward the same address and fails, the address is given up again at once. See Giving up an address.

give_up_pause. Measured from the timeout that gave the address up. Once it has passed, the echo may start one more trial toward the address, once the backoff has run out too. A reload applies a new value to an address already given up: the pause is measured from the same moment.

discovery_interval. The first fetch happens on the first cycle. After that a fetch starts when discovery_interval has passed since the last one started, or when a peer in RELAY without evidence asks for a refresh and at least 10 seconds have passed. Only one fetch runs at a time.

docs.title: Fixed values
docs.text:
These are not configurable.

Value Setting wg set time limit 2 s Underlay probe: ICMPv6 echo payload 16 bytes Probe nonce, the first bytes of every echo payload 8 random bytes Tunnel probe: whole IP packet the MTU of mesh_iface, read every cycle; never fragmented Discovery fetch time limit 5 s Discovery response size limit 65536 bytes Minimum gap between refresh-driven fetches 10 s Discovery server: request read time limit 2 s Discovery server: maximum request size 4096 bytes Discovery server: maximum open connections 16, of which at most 2 from one source address procd watchdog timeout (init script) 30 s procd respawn delay (init script) 5 s

For how these parameters shape behavior, see About the path state machine. To change them, see How to tune timing parameters.

docs.title: Service Commands
docs.text:
wgpathd is run and inspected through its init script, /etc/init.d/wgpathd, usually as service wgpathd <command>. Nothing is installed on the PATH.

Command Effect start Starts the daemon, if enabled is on and the configuration passes the config check. See start. stop Stops the daemon. restart stop, then start. Every peer starts again in RELAY. reload Applies a changed configuration to the running daemon. See reload. status Prints procd's state and, while running, a readable summary. See status. check Validates the configuration and the substrate. See check. migrate Moves peer settings left in /etc/config/network by releases up to 4 into /etc/config/wgpathd. See migrate. enable / disable Adds or removes the boot-time start link, /etc/rc.d/S95wgpathd.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
1. If option enabled in main is off, start registers the service with no instance and returns 0. The daemon does not run.
  2. Otherwise it runs the config check, /usr/libexec/wgpathd/check.uc --config. If that fails, the report and invalid configuration, not starting go to standard error and to syslog at daemon.err, no instance is created, and start returns 1. Nothing respawns.
  3. Otherwise procd starts /usr/libexec/wgpathd/daemon.uc as the instance wgpathd.

The config check only reads UCI. A failure that needs the running system, such as a WireGuard interface that is not up, still happens in the daemon, which then exits and is respawned every 5 seconds. See Log messages.

docs.title: reload
docs.text:
Situation Effect enabled is off Same as start: the service is left with no instance, so a running daemon stops. The daemon is not running Same as start. The daemon is running Runs the config check. If it passes, sends SIGHUP to the daemon. If it fails, the report and invalid configuration, keeping the running one go to standard error and to syslog, and the running daemon keeps its configuration. Returns 1.

procd runs reload by itself when it receives a config.change event for the wgpathd or network package. LuCI's Save & Apply and reload_config send that event; uci commit alone does not.

On SIGHUP the daemon reads /etc/config/wgpathd and /etc/config/network again:

What changed Effect role, mesh_iface, hub_iface, read_iface, serve_addr or serve_port The daemon logs reload: exiting for procd to start afresh changed=<option> and exits. procd starts it again after 5 seconds, and every peer starts in RELAY. Timing parameters Apply from the next cycle. mode Applies from the next cycle. Switching to observe demotes TRIALING and DIRECT peers to RELAY. discovery The new URL is fetched on the next cycle. The discovery map already held is kept until then. A peer's public_key, relay and tunnel all unchanged The peer keeps its state, counters and switch count. A peer rejected with relay routes into <mesh_iface> is guarded again, and becomes managed, starting in RELAY, if its route was fixed. A peer added, or one of those three options changed The peer is checked like at startup and, if managed, starts in RELAY. A peer removed It leaves steering and the status. Its endpoint is left as it is.

A spoke logs configuration reloaded peers_kept=<n> added=<n> removed=<n>, with mode=<mode> appended when the mode changed; a hub logs configuration reloaded. If the configuration is invalid when the daemon reads it, it logs reload: invalid configuration, keeping the running one: <CODE> (<detail>) and keeps running unchanged.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
The first line is procd's state of the service, and the exit status is procd's:

First line Exit status Meaning running 0 The daemon runs. active with no instances 0 The service is registered without a daemon, for example because enabled is off. inactive 3 The service is not registered with procd: stopped, or never started. not running 5 The instance exists but its process is not running, for example between respawns.

If enabled is off, the next line is disabled (option enabled in /etc/config/wgpathd). If the daemon runs, a summary of ubus call wgpathd status follows. If that call fails, wgpathd: cannot read status: <CODE> goes to standard error; the exit status is still procd's.

On a spoke:

running
role: spoke (mode steer)
discovery: fresh (last success 42s ago)
peers:
  spoke_b  SpokeBme  DIRECT  [2001:db8:b::20]:51820  5m ago (trial_ok)  2 switches
  spoke_c  SpokeCme  RELAY   10.10.0.13:51820        no change yet      0 switches
unmanaged:
  hub  HubMeshP  fixed endpoint
Line Content role: The role and the mode. discovery: fresh or stale, and the age of the last successful fetch, or never succeeded. peers: One line per managed peer, sorted by section: section, first 8 characters of the public key, state, asserted endpoint, age and reason of the last transition, and the switch count. peers: none when there are none. unmanaged: One line per unmanaged peer: section, key prefix, reason. Left out when there are none.

On a hub:

running
role: hub
published peers:
  SpokeAme  [2001:db8:a::1]:51820   handshake 12s ago
  SpokeBme  [2001:db8:b::20]:51820  handshake 7s ago

Each line is a key prefix, the published direct endpoint and the handshake age. published peers: none when the snapshot is empty.

Ages are shown in whole seconds, minutes, hours or days: 42s, 5m, 3h, 2d.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
service wgpathd check

It runs /usr/libexec/wgpathd/check.uc, which loads the configuration with the daemon's own loader and then checks the substrate the daemon needs. It changes nothing and works whether or not the daemon runs. Each finding is one line with a level:

Level Meaning ok The item is as it should be. skip The item was not checked, or is deliberately not steered. warn The daemon runs, but something is off or not ready yet. FAIL The daemon cannot start, or the item is a configuration mistake.

The exit status is 1 if any line is FAIL, 0 otherwise.

ok    config: spoke, mode observe, 1 steered peer, 2 not steered
ok    wg_mesh: up, 3 peers
ok    wg_hub: up, 1 peer
ok    peer spoke_b: relay 10.10.0.12:51820 via wg_hub, probes 10.20.0.12
skip  peer hub: not steered (fixed endpoint)
FAIL  peer spoke_c: not steered (invalid relay)
ok    firewall: ICMP echo-request (tunnel probe) from wg_mesh (zone vpn): accepted
warn  firewall: UDP port 51820 (relayed WireGuard) from wg_hub (zone vpn): no rule accepts it
      add it with:
        uci add firewall rule
        uci set firewall.@rule[-1].name='Allow-wgpathd-relay'
        uci set firewall.@rule[-1].src='vpn'
        uci set firewall.@rule[-1].proto='udp'
        uci set firewall.@rule[-1].dest_port='51820'
        uci set firewall.@rule[-1].target='ACCEPT'
        uci commit firewall
        service firewall reload
      or in /etc/config/firewall:
        config rule
            option name 'Allow-wgpathd-relay'
            option src 'vpn'
            option proto 'udp'
            option dest_port '51820'
            option target 'ACCEPT'
ok    firewall: ICMPv6 echo-request (underlay probe) from zone wan: accepted

A firewall warning that can name the rule to add is followed by it, indented, both as uci commands and as a section of /etc/config/firewall.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Level Line When ok config: spoke, mode <mode>, <n> steered peer(s), <n> not steered A valid spoke configuration. "Steered" counts peers with valid settings, before the route check. ok config: hub, reads <read_iface>, serves <addr>:<port> A valid hub configuration. FAIL config: option role must be 'spoke' or 'hub' (is <value>) role is missing or wrong. <value> is unset when missing. FAIL config: missing option <name> A required option is missing or empty. FAIL config: no interface <name> in /etc/config/network An interface option names no interface section. FAIL config: option <name> must be an interface name of letters, digits and _ mesh_iface, hub_iface or read_iface is not a plain section name. FAIL config: option discovery must be a URL of the form http://<host>[:<port>]/<path> discovery is not an http:// URL with a host, see UCI configuration. FAIL config: option serve_addr must be an IP address of the router, not unspecified or multicast serve_addr is not one literal address a listener can bind, see UCI configuration. FAIL config: option serve_port must be a port number from 1 to 65535 serve_port is not a decimal port number. FAIL config: option <name> must be a number from <min> to <max>, config: option <name> must be a whole number from <min> to <max> A timing parameter is not a decimal number within its bounds. FAIL config: option backoff_max must be at least backoff_min (<value>), config: option trial_window must be longer than cycle + tunnel_timeout (<sum>) On a spoke, two timing parameters disagree. warn config: unknown mode '<mode>' runs as observe mode is neither steer nor observe. warn service disabled (option enabled '<value>'): it will not start enabled is off. warn config: discovery host <name> is a name, not an address: every fetch waits for DNS The discovery URL names its host. The fetch looks it up without letting the daemon run meanwhile. warn config: discovery host <addr> routes via <oif>, not <hub_iface> The route to the discovery host does not leave via hub_iface, so discovery would stop with the path it goes over. Not checked with --config. warn config: discovery host <addr>: route lookup failed: <CODE> (<detail>) No route to the discovery host. Not checked with --config. warn config: serve_addr <addr> is no address of a WireGuard interface in /etc/config/network On a hub, no interface section with proto 'wireguard' lists serve_addr in its addresses. The discovery server then answers wherever the firewall lets that address be reached, and the check looks for no firewall rule for it; see Firewall rules. Not checked with --config. warn config: network section <section>: <options> left over from an earlier version, ignored; run service wgpathd migrate or remove it The section still has wgpathd_relay, wgpathd_tunnel or both, which releases up to 4 read and this one does not. <options> names them, joined by and; with two, the line ends remove them. See How to upgrade from a release that kept peer settings in the network configuration. warn peer settings for <key>: no such peer in <mesh_iface>, ignored On a spoke, a peer section's public_key is the key of no wireguard_<mesh_iface> section. warn peer settings without a public_key: ignored On a spoke, a peer section has no public_key. skip ubus unavailable: interfaces not checked ubus cannot be reached. The interface lines are left out; the peer lines still appear. ok <iface>: up, <n> peer(s) The interface is in the wireguard status reply. FAIL <iface>: <reason> mesh_iface or read_iface is not in the wireguard status reply, or the reply cannot be read. warn <hub_iface>: <reason> The same, for hub_iface. ok peer <section>: relay <relay> via <oif>, probes <tunnel> The peer is managed; the route to its relay host leaves via <oif>. FAIL peer <section>: relay routes into <mesh_iface> The relay host routes into the mesh. warn peer <section>: relay route lookup failed: <CODE> (<detail>) (retried every cycle) No route to the relay host yet. warn peer <section>: not in <mesh_iface> yet, skipped until it appears The peer is managed but not in the kernel's peer table. skip peer <section>: not steered (fixed endpoint) No peer section has the peer's key, and it has an endpoint_host in /etc/config/network, as the hub peer does. skip peer <section>: not steered (not configured) No peer section has the peer's key, and it has no endpoint_host. FAIL peer <section>: not steered (configured more than once) Two or more peer sections have the peer's key. FAIL peer <section>: not steered (missing <option>) The peer's peer section has no relay or no tunnel. FAIL peer <section>: not steered (invalid <option>) The peer's public_key in /etc/config/network, or the relay or tunnel of its peer section, is malformed.

The peer reasons are the ones in Managed and unmanaged peers.

The firewall lines come last, one for each traffic the role needs accepted, as Firewall rules describes. They are not checked with --config.

Level Line When ok firewall: <traffic> from <source>: accepted A rule, or the zone's input policy, accepts the traffic. warn firewall: <traffic> from <source>: no rule accepts it No rule accepts it, and the zone's policy rejects or drops it. The rule to add follows. warn firewall: <traffic> from <source>: a rule rejects it before any accepts it A rule with target 'REJECT' or 'DROP' decides it first. The rule to add follows; place it above the one that rejects. warn firewall: <traffic> from <iface> (no zone): no rule accepts it; put <iface> in a firewall zone The interface is in no zone, and the default input policy rejects the traffic. warn firewall: ICMPv6 echo-request (underlay probe) from zone wan: no rule accepts it: restore OpenWrt's default rule Allow-ICMPv6-Input On a spoke, nothing accepts ICMPv6 echo requests from wan. warn firewall: <traffic> from <source>: could not confirm, <reason> The check cannot tell. The rule to add follows when there is a zone and a port to name it by. skip firewall: no /etc/config/firewall, not checked There is no firewall configuration.

<traffic> is one of:

<traffic> Role option of the finding over ubus ICMP echo-request (tunnel probe), ICMPv6 echo-request (tunnel probe) Spoke, one line for each address family of mesh_iface mesh_iface UDP port <listen_port> (relayed WireGuard), or UDP (relayed WireGuard) without a listen_port Spoke hub_iface ICMPv6 echo-request (underlay probe) Spoke none TCP port <serve_port> (peer list) Hub, when a WireGuard interface holds serve_addr serve_port

<source> is <iface> (zone <zone>), <iface> (no zone) or, for the underlay probe, zone wan. <reason> is one of:

<reason> Cause a rule or zone option this check does not follow applies A rule that may decide the traffic, or the zone, has an option the check does not follow, such as src_ip or extra_src. the firewall has custom nftables rules An include section, or an nftables file fw4 includes, may add rules the check cannot read. a zone may take it by device or subnet A zone that matches by subnet, or by a network or device the check does not follow, such as an inverted one, may take the traffic before the interface's own. See Firewall rules. zone <zone> is not for IPv<n> The zone's family excludes the traffic's. <mesh_iface> has no listen_port The relay port is not fixed, so it cannot be looked for. no such zone There is no zone named wan.

The same findings, apart from the interface lines, are available over ubus, also for values not saved yet: see ubus config check.

docs.title: --config
docs.text: /usr/libexec/wgpathd/check.uc --config runs only the configuration findings: the config: lines, including the options left over in /etc/config/network, and the peer settings warnings, without the enabled warning, ubus, routes, the firewall or the other peer lines. It is what start and reload run. Any other argument prints usage: check.uc [--config] on standard error and exits with 2.

docs.title: migrate
docs.text:
service wgpathd migrate

It runs /usr/libexec/wgpathd/migrate.uc, the program the package's uci-defaults script runs after an install or upgrade: it moves the options wgpathd_relay and wgpathd_tunnel of every WireGuard peer section in /etc/config/network into the peer section with that peer's key in /etc/config/wgpathd, keeping any value already there, and commits both files. What it does, step by step, is in Files and dependencies.

Its messages go to syslog, and to standard error when run from a terminal; see Log messages. The exit status is 0 when everything was moved or there was nothing to move, and 1 when a step failed, in which case /etc/config/network is left as it was. It does not reload the daemon: run service wgpathd reload afterwards.

docs.title: WireGuard Substrate
docs.text: wgpathd reads the WireGuard setup from /etc/config/network and never writes it. It reads it at startup and again on every reload (service wgpathd reload). Its own settings, including those of each steered peer, are in /etc/config/wgpathd; see UCI configuration.

docs.title: What wgpathd reads from network
docs.text:
Read By For The interface sections named by mesh_iface, hub_iface or read_iface Both roles They must exist; see Validation order. Every section of type wireguard_<mesh_iface>, for example wireguard_wg_mesh: its name and public_key Spoke The mesh peers. Each is matched by public_key to a peer section of /etc/config/wgpathd, and named by its section name in logs, the status and the check. The addresses of every interface with proto 'wireguard' Hub, service wgpathd check only The warning when serve_addr is no address of a WireGuard interface. The options wgpathd_relay and wgpathd_tunnel of any section Both roles Only to warn that they are left over; see below.

wgpathd does not read endpoint, allowed_ips, the keys or any other option of a peer. A steered peer should have no endpoint option; wgpathd sets the endpoint at runtime.

The rpcd plugin's peers method reads the same peer sections, and returns only their names, public keys and descriptions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A spoke's peer section for spoke-b in /etc/config/network, and the peer section that makes wgpathd steer it, in /etc/config/wgpathd:

config wireguard_wg_mesh 'spoke_b'
    option public_key 'SpokeBmeshPublicKeyExample00000000000000000='
    list allowed_ips '10.12.0.0/16'
    list allowed_ips '10.20.0.12/32'
    option route_allowed_ips '1'

config peer
    option public_key 'SpokeBmeshPublicKeyExample00000000000000000='
    option relay      '10.10.0.12:51820'
    option tunnel     '10.20.0.12'

docs.title: Options left over from earlier releases
docs.text:
Releases up to 4 kept a peer's settings as the options wgpathd_relay and wgpathd_tunnel of its section in /etc/config/network. They are no longer read. The package moves them into /etc/config/wgpathd when it is installed or upgraded; see How to upgrade from a release that kept peer settings in the network configuration.

While a section still has either option, the daemon logs network section <section>: ignoring <options>, left over from an earlier version; run service wgpathd migrate once at startup, and service wgpathd check warns about it.

docs.title: Substrate requirements
docs.text:
wgpathd does not check these, but relaying and probing depend on them.

  • The relay host routes via the hub tunnel. The spoke's wg_hub peer for the hub must include the transit range (for example 10.10.0.0/24) in allowed_ips, with a route installed. No wg_mesh peer may include any transit address.
  • The hub forwards between its wg_hub peers within the transit range.
  • The wg_mesh listen port is fixed. The other spokes' relay endpoints name it. service wgpathd check warns when mesh_iface has no listen_port.
  • Relayed packets are accepted. They arrive on the spoke's wg_hub interface, addressed to the wg_mesh listen port. The firewall must accept them: see Firewall rules.
  • The tunnel address answers ping through wg_mesh, which the firewall must accept too: see Firewall rules.
  • The hub is a wg_mesh peer of every spoke, with a fixed IPv6 endpoint and a persistent keepalive, so the hub sees each spoke's current IPv6 endpoint. See About discovery.

How to prepare the WireGuard substrate shows a complete working layout.

docs.title: ubus Config Check
docs.text:
The package registers the ubus object wgpathd.config with three read-only methods:

Method Answers check The configuration check of service wgpathd check, for the saved configuration or for values that are not saved yet. peers The WireGuard interfaces, and the name, public key and description of each peer of one of them, and whether it has a fixed endpoint. schema Every timing parameter with its default and bounds. 
ubus call wgpathd.config check
ubus call wgpathd.config check '{"candidate": {"main": {"mode": "steer"}}}'
ubus call wgpathd.config peers
ubus call wgpathd.config schema

None of them changes anything. rpcd serves the object through the plugin /usr/share/rpcd/ucode/wgpathd.uc, so it answers whether or not the daemon runs, is enabled or has a valid configuration. rpcd loads the plugin when it starts or reloads; the package reloads rpcd when it is installed, upgraded or removed. The plugin reads the configuration afresh on every call.

Who may call it is up to rpcd's ACLs. The wgpathd package ships none; luci-app-wgpathd grants all three methods to its pages (see Files and dependencies). Grant them as you would grant reading the configuration. A caller learns from the replies what the router holds: the WireGuard interfaces, the section names, public keys and descriptions of their peers, which of them have a fixed endpoint, which peers have settings, through the relay and discovery route checks, whether the router would reach any address the caller puts in a candidate's relay or discovery, and by which interface, and, through the firewall lines, the firewall zones of the interfaces wgpathd uses and whether the firewall accepts wgpathd's traffic. It learns no private or preshared key, endpoint or allowed IP from /etc/config/network, and nothing else of /etc/config/firewall. The plugin reads both files itself, as root inside rpcd, so a caller needs no access to either.

docs.title: check
docs.text: check runs the full check of service wgpathd check, in the same order and with the same wording, except the lines that need ubus call wireguard status.

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text:
Included Left out The config: lines, and the loader failure if the configuration does not load <iface>: up, <n> peer(s) and the other interface lines service disabled (option enabled '<value>'): it will not start peer <section>: not in <mesh_iface> yet, skipped until it appears For a hub, whether serve_addr is an address of a WireGuard interface For a spoke, one line per peer: the relay route check of each steered peer and the reason each other one is not steered ubus unavailable: interfaces not checked The warnings about peer sections that match no mesh peer, and about options left over in /etc/config/network The firewall: lines, from /etc/config/firewall and the nftables files fw4 includes

The interface lines are left out because rpcd itself serves wireguard status, through rpcd-mod-wireguard, and cannot answer that call while it waits for it inside the plugin. For those lines, run service wgpathd check on the router.

The relay route of each steered peer is looked up in the router's routing table, as the daemon does at startup, and so is the route to the discovery host when the URL gives an address.

Each finding is described in Service commands.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Argument Type Description candidate object, optional Values to check instead of the saved ones. Without it, check checks /etc/config/wgpathd, /etc/config/network and /etc/config/firewall as service wgpathd check reads them.

rpcd refuses a candidate that is not an object, and any other argument, with Invalid argument (UBUS_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT).

docs.title: candidate
docs.text:
{
    "main": {
        "mode": "steer",
        "cycle": ""
    },
    "peers": {
        "O0LYRo/RVGHReCajupP1UioYUPELAkI8jPy1rWoazG4=": {
            "relay": "10.10.0.12:51820",
            "tunnel": "10.20.0.12"
        }
    }
}
Field Type Description main object, optional Options of the main section of /etc/config/wgpathd, by name. Any option name made of letters, digits and _. peers object, optional The peer sections of /etc/config/wgpathd, by public key. Each value is an object with relay, tunnel, or both.

Values are merged over the saved configuration, option by option:

  • An option given with a string replaces the saved value.
  • An option given as an empty string, "", removes the saved option, as clearing a field in a form does.
  • A number is taken as its decimal text: 45 is '45', 0.5 is '0.5'.
  • Any option not given keeps its saved value, including every option of a section the candidate does not name.
  • main may be given when /etc/config/wgpathd has no main section; its options then make up the whole section.
  • A peer is named by its WireGuard public key. Its values are merged over the peer section with that key; when there is none, they make up a new one. When several sections have the key, each gets the values.
  • A peer left with neither relay nor tunnel has no peer section, as clearing both fields of a peer in a form removes its section.
  • A key that is no peer of mesh_iface is accepted, and checked as a stale peer section. The candidate cannot change anything in /etc/config/network or /etc/config/firewall.
  • The merged values are checked as if they were saved: which peers are read depends on the merged mesh_iface, so a candidate that changes mesh_iface checks the peers of the new interface.

Nothing is written, staged or committed: a later call without candidate checks the saved configuration again. Changes staged but not committed with the uci command are part of the saved configuration here, as they are for service wgpathd check; changes staged in LuCI are not, since rpcd keeps them per session.

docs.text:

}
Field Type Description ok boolean false if any finding has the level fail; the exit status of service wgpathd check would be 1. findings array The findings, in the order service wgpathd check prints them.

docs.title: findings[]
docs.text:
Field Type Description level string ok, skip, warn or fail. service wgpathd check prints fail as FAIL. subject string config for the configuration and the enabled option, peer for a peer or a peer section, firewall for the firewall. (service wgpathd check also uses the interface name and ubus, for the lines left out here.) section string The section of /etc/config/network the finding is about: for peer, the peer's section; for config, a section with options left over from an earlier release. Left out for a peer section that matches no mesh peer. public_key string For peer, the peer's public key, when it is a valid key. It names the peer's peer section in /etc/config/wgpathd. option string Present when the finding is about one option: the loader failures that name one (role, a missing option, an option with an invalid value), mode for an unknown mode, enabled, discovery for the warnings about the discovery host, serve_addr for a listener address outside the WireGuard interfaces, and for a peer the option of its peer section that is missing or malformed (relay, tunnel), relay for a relay routed into the mesh, or public_key for a peer in /etc/config/network without a valid key; for the firewall, the option the traffic follows from: mesh_iface for the tunnel probe, hub_iface for relayed packets, serve_port for the peer list. Left out otherwise, for example for no interface <name> in /etc/config/network, configured more than once or the underlay probe. message string The line service wgpathd check prints after the level, word for word. fix object For a firewall finding that is not ok, when there is a zone and a port to name: the rule that would accept the traffic. service wgpathd check prints it under the line. Left out otherwise. fix.uci string The rule as uci commands, one per line, ending with uci commit firewall and service firewall reload. fix.config string The same rule as a config rule section of /etc/config/firewall, one line per option, indented with a tab.

section, public_key and option name UCI sections and options, so a client can attach a finding to the field it is about; message and fix are for showing, as text. The firewall messages and rules hold names from /etc/config/firewall and /etc/config/network; zone names are only those fw4 accepts, letters, digits and _./-.

docs.title: Malformed candidate
docs.text:
A candidate that does not follow the rules above is not checked. The reply is:

{
    "error": "CHECK_INVALID_CANDIDATE",
    "message": "peers: 'spoke_b' is not a WireGuard public key"
}
message Cause candidate must be an object candidate is not an object. unknown part '<name>' candidate has a field other than main and peers. main must be an object, peers must be an object, peers.<key> must be an object A part is not an object. main: unknown option '<name>' An option name with characters other than letters, digits and _. peers: '<key>' is not a WireGuard public key A peer is named by anything but a public key: 43 base64 characters followed by =. peers.<key>: unknown option '<name>' A peer option other than relay and tunnel, including public_key and the wgpathd_relay and wgpathd_tunnel of earlier releases. main.<name> must be a string or a number, peers.<key>.<name> must be a string or a number A value is a boolean, an array or an object.

docs.title: peers
docs.text:
Lists the WireGuard interfaces of /etc/config/network, and the peers of one of them, for a client that must name the peers without reading /etc/config/network, which holds every private key of the router.

ubus call wgpathd.config peers
ubus call wgpathd.config peers '{"iface": "wg_hub"}'

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Argument Type Description iface string, optional The interface whose peers to list: the name of an interface section with proto 'wireguard'. Without it, the interface of the saved role: mesh_iface on a spoke, read_iface on a hub.

An iface that is not the plain name of a WireGuard interface, the empty string included, is answered { "error": "PEERS_INVALID_IFACE", "message": "iface must name a WireGuard interface of /etc/config/network" }, and no peer is read.

docs.title: Reply
docs.text:
{
    "iface": "wg_mesh",
    "interfaces": [ "wg_hub", "wg_mesh" ],
    "peers": [
        { "section": "spoke_b", "public_key": "O0LYRo/RVGHReCajupP1UioYUPELAkI8jPy1rWoazG4=", "description": "beach" },
        { "section": "hub", "public_key": "W+1CXUTTLNuEuF+fANM4a1F4kUcjzH1oH9VYWI9eA00=", "fixed_endpoint": true }
    ]
}
Field Type Description iface string or null The interface listed. null when no iface was given and the saved role names no WireGuard interface, for example while role is unset; peers is then empty. interfaces array of strings Every interface section with proto 'wireguard', sorted by name. peers array Every section of type wireguard_<iface>, in the order of /etc/config/network. peers[].section string The section name; for an anonymous section, the id UCI gave it, such as cfg09cdcd. peers[].public_key string or null The peer's public_key as written, or null when it has none. peers[].description string The peer's description, when it has one. peers[].fixed_endpoint boolean true when the peer has a non-empty endpoint_host, as the hub peer does; absent otherwise. The endpoint itself is not given. wgpathd leaves such a peer alone unless it has a peer section.

Nothing else of a peer or an interface is returned: no private or preshared key, endpoint, allowed IP, listen port or address.

docs.title: schema
docs.text:
Lists the timing parameters the main section takes, for a client that builds a form from them rather than from a list of its own. The Timing tab of the LuCI settings page is built from it.

{
    "parameters": [
        { "name": "cycle", "default": 3, "min": 1, "max": 10, "whole": false },
        { "name": "n_up", "default": 5, "min": 1, "max": 100, "whole": true }
    ]
}
Field Type Description parameters array Every parameter, in the order of Timing parameters. parameters[].name string The option name. parameters[].default number The value used when the option is not set. parameters[].min, parameters[].max number The bounds, both included. parameters[].whole boolean true when only whole numbers are taken.

The bounds alone do not make a valid set: on a spoke some parameters must also agree, which only check tells. See Timing parameters.

docs.title: ubus Status
docs.text:
While it runs, wgpathd registers the ubus object wgpathd with one method, status. It takes no arguments and changes nothing; it accepts and ignores the ubus_rpc_session argument that uhttpd adds to calls from LuCI.

ubus call wgpathd status

If the daemon is not running, ubus reports Command failed: Not found.

This is the machine-readable interface. service wgpathd status prints a readable summary of the same reply; see Service commands.

The reply depends on the role. Fields that have no value yet are null.

docs.title: Times
docs.text:
Every time in the reply is an integer Unix time in seconds, from the router's clock: now, discovery.last_ok, and each peer's since, trial_deadline, next_trial, given_up.since, given_up.until, last_change.ts and history[].ts. now is the router's time when it answered, so a client computes an age as now - ts and a wait as ts - now, whatever its own clock says: since 1790456470 with now 1790456500 is 30 seconds ago, next_trial 1790456530 is in 30 seconds.

Apart from discovery.last_ok, these times are kept on the monotonic clock and converted when the reply is built, against the same now. A step of the router's wall clock, such as NTP setting it after boot, therefore shifts them all together and leaves every difference to now correct. discovery.last_ok is read from the wall clock when the fetch succeeds, so it does not move with such a step.

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Field Type Description role string spoke. mode string steer or observe. An unknown configured mode shows as observe. now integer Unix time when the reply was built. See Times. mesh_iface string The configured mesh_iface. hub_iface string The configured hub_iface. params object The timing parameters in effect, defaults and overrides merged, as numbers: cycle, n_up, m_down, tunnel_timeout, trial_window, backoff_min, backoff_max, backoff_reset, discovery_interval, give_up_after, give_up_pause. See Timing parameters. discovery object Discovery state; see below. peers object One entry per managed peer, keyed by its wg_mesh public key. unmanaged array Peers wgpathd does not steer; see below. history array The most recent state changes across all peers, newest first; see below.

docs.title: discovery
docs.text: Field Type Description fresh boolean true if the most recent completed fetch succeeded. false before the first fetch completes and after any failed fetch. last_ok integer or null Unix time of the last successful fetch. null until one succeeds. Loading the cache at startup does not set it. url string The configured discovery URL: the scheme, host, port and path only: never the user:password@ part, the query or the fragment. A value that does not read as scheme://host[:port] shows as (unreadable url).

docs.title: peers.<pubkey>
docs.text:
Field Type Description state string RELAY, TRIALING or DIRECT. section string The UCI section name of the peer in /etc/config/network. up_streak integer Consecutive cycles with direct evidence, counted in RELAY. down_streak integer Consecutive failed tunnel probes, counted in DIRECT. A probe answered over the relay counts as failed. backoff number Current backoff interval in seconds; 0 means none. This is the interval, not the time remaining. ready boolean true when up_streak has reached n_up, or in RELAY on a cycle that saw an authenticated roam; false while the echo points at an address that is given up (see given_up), since steer mode would not trial it. In observe mode this means steer mode would start a trial. In steer mode it can stay true while a backoff is still running. endpoint string or null The endpoint wgpathd asserted on the last decided cycle: the relay endpoint in RELAY, the target otherwise. null before the first cycle. It is what wgpathd asked for, even if that wg set failed, and can differ from the kernel's current endpoint after a roam. target string or null The direct endpoint being trialed or held. null in RELAY. candidate string or null The peer's direct endpoint in the discovery map: from the last successful fetch, or from the cache until one succeeds. null if the map has none. A trial takes this endpoint, unless the peer roamed to another direct address first, or it is refused. candidate_refused string or null Why candidate is not taken for this peer, as of the last cycle: own address, relay address, tunnel address or routes into <iface>; see Discovery HTTP API. null when it is taken, when there is none, and before the first cycle. last_target string or null The direct endpoint most recently trialed or held, kept after the peer falls back to RELAY: in RELAY after a trial_timeout or demoted, the address that failed. It follows roams while DIRECT. null until the first trial since the peer started being managed. since integer Unix time when the current state began: the last transition, or, before any, when the peer started being managed. trial_deadline integer or null In TRIALING, the Unix time at which the trial times out unless an answer proves it first. null in the other states. next_trial integer or null In RELAY in steer mode, while a backoff runs, the Unix time it ends: the earliest a trial can start. The trial also needs the peer to be ready. null otherwise: no backoff running, another state, or observe mode. failed_target string or null The direct endpoint whose trials timed out, the last failed_trials of them in a row. null before any trial timed out, and after a trial commits. failed_trials integer Trials in a row that timed out on failed_target; 0 when it is null. A timeout on another target starts again at 1. Demotions are not counted. given_up object or null Set while failed_target is given up: it reached give_up_after failed trials, and the underlay echo alone starts no trial toward it. null otherwise. See Giving up an address. switches integer Number of state transitions since the daemon started, or since a reload added the peer or changed its settings. Roam adoptions are not counted. relayed_answers integer Tunnel probe answers after which the kernel endpoint was the relay, over the same span as switches. It grows while the peer's side is in RELAY and sends traffic, whose packets move the kernel endpoint back onto the relay. Such an answer does not commit a trial but does hold DIRECT, so a count that keeps growing while the peer is DIRECT can mean a direct path that no longer carries traffic. last_change object or null The most recent state transition; null if none since the peer started being managed.

state, up_streak, down_streak, backoff and ready are updated at the end of each cycle in which the peer was decided. A peer skipped in a cycle (missing from the kernel, or while wireguard status cannot be read) keeps its previous values.

docs.title: peers.<pubkey>.given_up
docs.text: Field Type Description since integer Unix time of the trial timeout that gave the address up. until integer since plus give_up_pause: from then on the echo may start one more trial toward the address, the backoff permitting. A roam, or another address from discovery that answers the echo, starts a trial sooner. It stays set, possibly in the past, until a trial starts.

docs.title: peers.<pubkey>.last_change
docs.text: Field Type Description ts integer Unix time of the transition. from string Previous state. to string New state. reason string One of the reasons below. Reason Transition trial_start RELAY → TRIALING trial_ok TRIALING → DIRECT trial_timeout TRIALING → RELAY demoted DIRECT → RELAY after m_down failed probes observe_mode TRIALING or DIRECT → RELAY because the mode is not steer

docs.title: history[]
docs.text:
The last 20 transitions and roam adoptions of all managed peers, newest first; entries in the same cycle are listed in reverse peer order. Giving an address up, and resuming trials, change no path and are not listed: the trial timeout before a give-up is, and the peer's given_up and the log show the rest. It is kept in memory: a restart of the daemon, including the one a structural reload causes, empties it. A reload that removes or changes a peer keeps its entries.

Field Type Description ts integer Unix time of the change. For a transition it equals the peer's last_change.ts. section string The peer's UCI section name in /etc/config/network, when the change happened. pubkey string The peer's public key. from string Previous state. to string New state. For a roam adoption, DIRECT, like from. reason string One of the reasons of a transition, or roam_adopted: a DIRECT peer followed an authenticated roam to another direct address, which switches does not count. endpoint string The endpoint asserted after the change: the relay endpoint after a change to RELAY, the direct target otherwise. The same as endpoint= in the log line for the change.

docs.title: unmanaged[]
docs.text: Field Type Description section string The UCI section name of the peer in /etc/config/network. Anonymous sections show their generated name, such as cfg0a8f3c. pubkey string or null The peer's public_key as configured; null if it has none. reason string Why the peer is not managed. See Managed and unmanaged peers.

docs.title: UCI Configuration
docs.text:
wgpathd reads /etc/config/wgpathd at startup and again on every service wgpathd reload. Most options apply on reload; role and the interface and listener options restart the daemon. The full list is in Service commands.

The service options live in one section of type wgpathd named main. On a spoke, each mesh peer to steer has a section of type peer as well; see Peer sections. Sections of other types are ignored.

What wgpathd reads from /etc/config/network is listed in WireGuard substrate.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
Option Required Default Values enabled No on 0, no, off, false or disabled turn it off; anything else, or no value, leaves it on.

While it is off, service wgpathd start starts no daemon, service wgpathd reload stops a running one, and service wgpathd check warns. The daemon itself does not read this option.

docs.title: role
docs.text:
Option Required Values role Yes spoke or hub

Any other value, or no value, stops startup with CONFIG_INVALID_ROLE. The detail is the value given, or unset.

docs.title: Spoke options
docs.text:
config wgpathd 'main'
    option role       'spoke'
    option mesh_iface 'wg_mesh'
    option hub_iface  'wg_hub'
    option discovery  'http://10.10.0.1:7780/peers'
    option mode       'observe'
Option Required Default Description mesh_iface Yes — The WireGuard interface whose peer endpoints are steered. Must be a name of letters, digits and _, and a network section of type interface, and must appear in the ubus call wireguard status reply at startup. Its peers are read from wireguard_<mesh_iface> sections. hub_iface Yes — The hub tunnel interface. Must be a name of letters, digits and _, and a network section of type interface. Checked at startup only; wgpathd does not otherwise use it. discovery Yes — URL of the hub's discovery endpoint, for example http://10.10.0.1:7780/peers: http://, in lower case, a host, an optional port from 1 to 65535, and a path. https is refused: the daemon has no TLS context to fetch it with. A host name is accepted, but service wgpathd check warns about it, because the fetch waits for its DNS lookup, and the full check warns when the host's route does not leave via hub_iface. See Discovery HTTP API. mode No observe steer lets wgpathd move peers to direct paths. observe keeps every managed peer on its relay endpoint. Any other value runs as observe and logs a warning at startup and on reload.

docs.title: Hub options
docs.text:
config wgpathd 'main'
    option role       'hub'
    option read_iface 'wg_mesh'
    option serve_addr '10.10.0.1'
    option serve_port '7780'
Option Required Default Description read_iface Yes — The WireGuard interface whose peer endpoints are published. Must be a name of letters, digits and _, and a network section of type interface, and must appear in the ubus call wireguard status reply at startup. serve_addr Yes — Local address the discovery listener binds to: one literal IPv4 or IPv6 address, which wgpathd uses in its canonical form. A host name, the wildcard addresses 0.0.0.0 and ::, a multicast or broadcast address, and an IPv6 link-local address (which needs a zone) are refused. service wgpathd check warns when it is not an address of a WireGuard interface. serve_port Yes — TCP port of the discovery listener: a decimal number from 1 to 65535, without spaces, leading zeros or other notations. The firewall must accept it from the hub tunnel; see Firewall rules.

The hub ignores mode.

docs.title: Peer sections
docs.text:
On a spoke, each mesh peer that wgpathd steers has one section of type peer. The section is found by the peer's public key, so it may be anonymous, and it does not follow a rename of the peer's section in /etc/config/network. A hub reads no peer section.

config peer
    option public_key 'SpokeBmeshPublicKeyExample00000000000000000='
    option relay      '10.10.0.12:51820'
    option tunnel     '10.20.0.12'
Option Required Format Description public_key Yes WireGuard public key: 43 base64 characters followed by = The key of a peer section of type wireguard_<mesh_iface> in /etc/config/network. relay Yes Endpoint: v4:port or [v6]:port, port 1–65535 The endpoint used on the relay path: the peer's address on the hub tunnel and the peer's wg_mesh listen port. Its route must leave via an interface other than mesh_iface. tunnel Yes IPv4 or IPv6 address, no port The peer's address inside wg_mesh. Target of the tunnel probe. Must be inside the peer's allowed_ips.

Endpoints and addresses are used in canonical form (lowercase, compressed IPv6), so [2001:DB8::0001]:51820 and [2001:db8::1]:51820 are the same.

A peer section whose public_key is no peer of mesh_iface, or that has no public_key, is stale: wgpathd ignores it, and service wgpathd check warns about it with peer settings for <key>: no such peer in <mesh_iface>, ignored or peer settings without a public_key: ignored.

Releases up to 4 kept relay and tunnel as the options wgpathd_relay and wgpathd_tunnel of the peer's section in /etc/config/network. Those options are no longer read. The package moves them here on upgrade; see How to upgrade from a release that kept peer settings in the network configuration.

docs.title: Managed and unmanaged peers
docs.text:
A mesh peer is managed when it has exactly one peer section, with a valid relay and tunnel, and the route to its relay address leaves via an interface other than mesh_iface. wgpathd steers only managed peers.

Any other peer of mesh_iface is unmanaged: wgpathd never touches its endpoint. Unmanaged peers are logged at startup and on reload, reported by service wgpathd check, and listed in the unmanaged array of ubus call wgpathd status. The checks run in this order; the first failure is the reason reported.

Reason Cause Check level Rechecked invalid public_key The peer's public_key in /etc/config/network is missing or not a valid key FAIL On reload not configured No peer section has the peer's key, and the peer has no endpoint_host skip On reload fixed endpoint No peer section has the peer's key, and the peer has an endpoint_host, as the hub peer does skip On reload configured more than once Two or more peer sections have the peer's key FAIL On reload missing relay The peer section has no relay FAIL On reload invalid relay relay is not a valid v4:port or [v6]:port FAIL On reload missing tunnel The peer section has no tunnel FAIL On reload invalid tunnel tunnel is not a valid IP address FAIL On reload relay routes into <mesh_iface> The route to the relay host leaves via mesh_iface FAIL On reload relay route lookup failed: <error> The route lookup for the relay host failed, for example because wg_hub is not up yet warn Every cycle

Every reload reads the peer sections again and repeats the route check, so fixing a peer and reloading is enough. A peer waiting on a failed route lookup is also rechecked at the start of every cycle. Either way, a peer whose relay route now leaves via another interface becomes managed, starting in RELAY, and wgpathd logs relay route found, now managed. A waiting peer whose route resolves into mesh_iface becomes unmanaged with relay routes into <mesh_iface>.

The spoke's own wg_mesh peer for the hub has a fixed endpoint, endpoint_host in /etc/config/network, and no peer section, so it is always listed as unmanaged with fixed endpoint. That is expected: the hub peer keeps its fixed endpoint.

A fixed endpoint alone does not keep wgpathd away. A peer with an endpoint_host and a peer section is steered like any other: a roamer may give an anchor its stable address as endpoint_host, so that the two meet without wgpathd too, and steer it as well. netifd sets the fixed endpoint when the interface comes up, and wgpathd replaces it with the relay endpoint or a direct address from then on. Never give the hub peer a peer section: wgpathd would then move the hub's own endpoint.

docs.title: Timing parameters
docs.text:
Both roles accept the timing parameters as options in the main section, for example option cycle '2'. Each is optional and overrides one default. The full list, defaults and meanings are in Timing parameters.

A parameter value must be a decimal number: digits, optionally followed by a dot and more digits, within the parameter's bounds; n_up, m_down and give_up_after take whole numbers only. 3, 2.5 and 900 are in that form; -1, 1e3, 0x10 and 3s are not. On a spoke, backoff_max must be at least backoff_min and trial_window longer than cycle plus tunnel_timeout. An invalid value stops startup with CONFIG_INVALID_OPTION; the detail names the parameter and what it must be, for example cycle must be a number from 1 to 10. The bounds are in Timing parameters.

docs.title: Validation order
docs.text:
The configuration is checked in this order, by the daemon at startup and on reload, and by service wgpathd check. The first failure is the one reported. At startup it stops the daemon with exit status 1 and an invalid configuration: log message; service wgpathd start and reload run the same check first and refuse to start or reload.

  1. role is spoke or hub — else CONFIG_INVALID_ROLE.
  2. Every required option for the role is a non-empty string — else CONFIG_MISSING_OPTION naming the first missing option, in the order listed above.
  3. Every required option has the form it must have, in the order listed above — else CONFIG_INVALID_OPTION. An interface option is a name of letters, digits and _: UCI's other ways to address a section, such as @interface[0], are refused, and the value is looked up only as a name. On a spoke, discovery is checked, and on a hub serve_addr and serve_port, as described above.
  4. Every interface option names a network section of type interface — else INTERFACE_MISSING naming the value.
  5. Every timing parameter present is within its bounds, in the order of Timing parameters, and on a spoke the parameters agree — else CONFIG_INVALID_OPTION.

On a spoke, the mesh peers are then loaded with their peer sections. A peer with a problem does not stop startup; it is reported as unmanaged. See Managed and unmanaged peers.

docs.title: Shipped default
docs.text: The package installs /etc/config/wgpathd with option enabled '0' and no other active option. It holds a commented-out example for each role, for a timing override and for a peer section. With it, the service does not start, and service wgpathd check fails with option role must be 'spoke' or 'hub' (is unset). It is a conffile: an upgrade keeps your edits.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Tutorials are lessons. Each takes you step by step through a complete piece of work, so you learn by doing it.

  • Your First Failover - Configure wgpathd on a hub and two spokes in a lab of OpenWrt containers, watch both spokes go direct, then cut the direct path and watch the relay carry the traffic.
  • Developer Onboarding - Run the test suite, explore the decision core's tests, build the package and check it installs on a fresh OpenWrt.

Once you have done the lab, set up wgpathd on real routers with the operator how-to guides, starting with preparing the WireGuard substrate.

docs.title: Developer Onboarding
docs.text:
In this tutorial we will run wgpathd's test suite, look at the tests for its decision core, build the OpenWrt package, and check that the package installs cleanly on a fresh OpenWrt. By the end we will have a working development loop and a package file we built ourselves.

Everything runs in Docker containers based on official OpenWrt images. Nothing gets installed on our machine.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker, with permission to run containers as our user.
  • make.
  • A copy of the wgpathd repository.
  • About 6 GB of free disk space for the images, most of it for the OpenWrt SDK, and a network connection for the first run.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the repository
docs.text:
We start in the root of the repository:

cd wgpathd
ls

We should see, among others, src/, test/, files/, openwrt/ and a Makefile. The daemon's code is in src/wgpathd/; the files the package installs on a router are in files/.

docs.title: Step 2: Run the whole test suite
docs.text:
make test

The first time, this builds a development image from the OpenWrt rootfs and installs ucode, its modules and the utest test runner into it. That takes a few minutes and prints Docker build output. Later runs start in seconds.

Then the tests run. Each dot is one passing test, grouped by bundle, and the run ends with a summary like this:

Summary:

  293 successes / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped / 0 ignored (11945 ms)
  Seed:   1790466118615660777

The exact count grows as tests are added. What matters is 0 failures / 0 errors. Notice the seed: some tests generate random inputs, and the seed identifies this run.

docs.title: Step 3: Look at the decision core's tests
docs.text:
wgpathd makes every path decision in one pure function, decide. Let's run only its tests, with one line per test:

make unit MODULES=test/unit/wgpathd/decide_test.uc VERBOSE=1

This time we see test names:

[test/unit/wgpathd/decide_test.uc] test/unit/wgpathd/decide_test.uc (61 tests)
  [PASS] anchor: echo fails but an authenticated roam promotes with the roam as target
  [PASS] lying hub: a bogus candidate fails its trial and backs off
  [PASS] trial false positive: echo ok but the tunnel never answers
  ...

Notice the names such as anchor and lying hub. Each one is a situation wgpathd must survive, from When things fail, so the tests read like that list. The ones starting with I1, I4 or I5 are the property tests that use random inputs; each number is an invariant listed in How the core is tested.

Now let's run just the tests with "roam" in their name:

make unit FILTER='roam'

The summary shows only a dozen or so successes; the tests that did not match are counted as ignored. FILTER and MODULES are how we keep the loop fast while working on one area.

docs.title: Step 4: Check the code compiles
docs.text:
make lint

This compiles every ucode file and syntax-checks every shell script. It prints nothing when all is well. CI runs make lint and make test on every push.

docs.title: Step 5: Build the package
docs.text:
make package

The first run builds an image from the OpenWrt SDK and fetches feed metadata; this takes longer than the test image did. At the end we should see a line like:

'bin/packages/x86_64/base/wgpathd-0.1.0-r8.apk' -> '/artifacts/wgpathd-0.1.0-r8.apk'

Let's confirm the file is there:

ls bin/

wgpathd-0.1.0-r8.apk

That is the package an operator installs on a hub or a spoke.

docs.title: Step 6: Install it on a fresh OpenWrt
docs.text:
make package-check

This rebuilds the package, installs it offline into an OpenWrt rootfs container that already has its dependencies, and runs a list of checks, including an upgrade from an earlier release that loaded firewall rules of its own. Among the lines it prints are these, and it ends with the last one:

ok   shipped disabled
     -> err: invalid configuration: CONFIG_INVALID_ROLE (unset)
ok   daemon with default config fails cleanly
     -> FAIL  config: option role must be 'spoke' or 'hub' (is unset)
ok   config check fails cleanly on the example
     -> wgpathd: cannot read status: UBUS_CONNECT_FAILED
ok   status without a daemon fails cleanly
ok   full check passes a valid config without ubus
ok   full check prints the firewall rule the hub needs
ok   init script enables
ok   only install and upgrade may reload fw4
ok   upgrade restarts a running daemon
ok   package scripts parse
ok   package removes cleanly
ok   a release with the fw4 include, its rules loaded
ok   upgrade from a release with the fw4 include
ok   upgrade removed the include
ok   upgrade unloaded its rules
package-check: all passed

Notice the three lines starting with ->. The shipped configuration names no role, and the container has no ubus, so nothing can really start. The check makes sure each tool says so in one clear line instead of crashing. The second one, FAIL config: option role must be 'spoke' or 'hub' (is unset), is exactly what an operator sees from service wgpathd check on a router where wgpathd is installed but not configured yet.

docs.title: What we did
docs.text: We ran the full test suite in an OpenWrt container, looked at the decision core's tests and how they map to the failures wgpathd must survive, narrowed a run with MODULES and FILTER, built the .apk in the OpenWrt SDK, and proved it installs and fails safely on a clean system.
